articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Junctionless Finfet For Hydrogen Sensing Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The junctionless FinFET (JL-FinFET) exhibits excellent scalability, low power consumption, and high sensitivity, making it a promising candidate for hydrogen sensing applications. A thorough performance analysis of the JL-FinFET for applications involving hydrogen sensing is analysed in this paper. It is evident that the gate material of JLFinFET significantly influences its sensitivity, with palladium (Pd) and Platinum (Pt) being the most promising gate materials for applications involving hydrogen sensing. The modulation of JL-FinFET’s hydrogen sensing performance is largely dependent on work function. Hydrogen molecule adsorption on the gate material modifies the work function, which impacts the device’s threshold voltage and drain current. Our analytical model accurately describes the hydrogen sensing behaviour of JL-FinFET and takes into account the work function modulation effect. Our study’s conclusions offer important direction for creating JL-FinFET hydrogen sensors with improved selectivity and sensitivity. We study the effect of different pressures from $10^{-14}$ torr to $\mathbf{1 0}^{-10}$ torr on JL-FinFET’s hydrogen sensing performance, including conductance, drain current, and threshold voltage. Our findings demonstrate that JL-FinFET can achieve fast response time and high hydrogen sensitivity.

articleTitle: Learn Feature Representation from Unlabeled Data using Self-Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In the recent past, promising performance is achieved by supervised deep learning networks in various domains like computer vision, machine translation, speech recognition, natural language processing (NLP), etc. But current deep-learning approaches required a large amount of manual data to achieve promising performance. However, manual annotation of data is time-consuming and needs human expertise, which is always not possible in a domain like healthcare. Recently an alternative method called Self Supervised Learning (SSL), uses unlabeled data and does not require manual annotation. With the help of a pretext task, SSL extracts and learns features from the unlabeled data, enabling models trained for these tasks to acquire latent representations that enhance subsequent tasks like object detection and classification. In this work, the unlabeled data is fed to the convolution neural network (CNN), which learns features and transfers them to the downstream task to generate the labeled data. The experiments are conducted on the fashion MNIST dataset in a self-supervised learning environment and a comparison is made with a different size of training data and the rotation pretext task approach is compared with SimCLR approach of contrastive learning which achieve state-of-art performance. Another experiment performs on Chest X-ray dataset, COVID-19 CT Scan dataset using SimCLR and other methods of contrastive learning. The experiment concludes that contrastive learning of self-supervised learning achieves better performance over rotation pretext task of self-supervised learning. The self-supervised learning environment is preferable in various domains where human annotation for labeling datasets is very costly or not feasible.

articleTitle: Advancing Digital Forensics: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Deepfake Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Deepfake has significantly advanced the generation of synthetic media capabilities, allowing for the creation of significantly promising fake visual and audio content. This technology manipulates existing media to replace a person’s face and voice, posing severe ethical and security concerns. Deepfakes are increasingly exploited in various cybercrimes, including identity theft, cyber extortion, and the spread of fake news, with over 95% involving obscene content highlighting the growing threat. Hence, the detection of deepfake content is a growing field among researchers. Moving on the same lines, our study compared the six well-known models (i.e., MesoNet, Xception, VGG19, ResNet101, NAS-Net, and MobileNet). A dataset was used that has both real and fake images which was employed for all models to assess their performance. Our results showed that the VGG19 was the most effective model with 83.84% among all six. The results can be used to further push the development of tools and techniques to fight against the digital media tampering that may be helpful for the cybersecurity industry.

articleTitle: Classification of Rice Variant using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Rice is a popular crop in the world. This paper has constructed a model using deep Learning for classification. Classification is a critical process in identifying the class of an image. Here, the Rice dataset has been taken to classify the class of rice Breed. Image Classification is a complex process that is affected by various factors. The emphasis is placed on summarizing essential superior class procedures and the strategies used for improving classification accuracy. This paper uses the deep learning approach for classification, such as CNN, and some activation functions, such as ReLu Softmax with Dense layers. The classification process used various domains, such as Machine Learning and deep learning. In this model, five classes of rice breed have been taken and classified with an accuracy of ${9 6 \%}$.

articleTitle: AI-Enabled IoT Framework for Sustainable and Autonomous Irrigation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Traditional farming methods are hindered by inefficient resource usage and inadequate crop management due to limited access to real-time data on soil conditions and environmental factors. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) in Smart Agriculture is transforming conventional farming methods. This research introduces an Optimized Agriculture System leveraging Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) technologies. The system collects real-time data from agricultural areas by integrating sensors with NodeMCU microcontrollers implemented as part of a Wireless Sensor Network (WSN). A Smart Irrigation machine learning (ML) model deployed on the edge determines an optimal irrigation schedule based on sensor data, ensuring crop health and efficient water utilization. The proposed Smart Agriculture System optimizes agricultural practices through AI and IoT integration, aiming to enhance crop yield, resource efficiency, and overall farm productivity.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Speed Control of Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) for Vehicular Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) has emerged as a viable alternative for vehicular applications due to its simple built and Sturdiness. This paper provides a comprehensive comparative analysis of speed control techinquest employed in SRMs, specifically focusing on hysteresis current control, PI control, and vector control methods. Each technique is systematically examined to evaluate its effectiveness in maintaining precise speed regulation under varying operational conditions. The mathematical models for each control strategy are implemented in MATLAB, allowing for simulation and performance evaluation. Results are presented to illustrate the response characteristics of the SRM across different control approaches, highlighting the trade-offs between speed, accuracy, rippling torque, and responsiveness. This study underscores the importance of selecting appropriate speed control methods for optimizing the operation of SRMs in electric vehicles. The findings contribute to the existing body of knowledge by identifying optimal control strategies that align with the evolving demands of modern vehicular applications, ultimately aiding in the advancement of more efficient and responsive electric drive.

articleTitle: Analysis of Stability, Speed and Power Dissipation of Different SRAM cells at 45nm Technology Node
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Contemporary applications that depend on system-on-chip technology require SRAMs that provide not just high speed and stability, but also energy efficiency for extended periods of operation. This study investigates several designs of SRAM cells, analyzing aspects such as power leakage, delays in reading and writing operations, and the static noise margins (WSNM and RSNM). Simulations revealed that of the studied topologies, the 10T SRAM cell demonstrated the highest RSNM, whereas the 8T SRAM cell exhibited greater WSNM due to its p-type access transistors. In addition, the write delay is reduced in the 8T SRAM cell in comparison to other designs. In addition, the standard 6T and 10T SRAM cells have the lowest amount of leakage power compared to all the simulated topologies. The SRAM bit cells were fabricated utilizing the gpdk 45 nm technology in the Cadence Virtuoso tool.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection using YOLO v7 and YOLO v8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The architecture of the brain is incredibly complex, with multiple areas managing various parts of the nervous system. An adult’s health is greatly at risk from brain tumors because of their ability to severely impair organ function or possibly cause death due to their rapid growth of abnormal brain cells. Brain tumors can develop in any area of the skull or brain, including the protective layer around the brain and many other areas. Since these tumors can have a wide range of shapes, sizes, and locations, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an essential tool for locating malignant tumors. MRIs are examined manually in order to diagnose brain tumors. However, manually identifying brain tumors is a challenging and time-consuming task that may result in errors. As a result, computer-aided brain tumor detection has been considered a crucial area of study in biomedical engineering. However, because tumor sizes and shapes vary enormously throughout subjects, developing a reliable brain tumor detector remains difficult. Thus, for the purpose of accurately identifying brain tumors in MRI scans, two popular deep learning detection algorithms—YOLO v7 and YOLO v8—were tested and compared in this study. From the results, YOLO v8 model has achieved highest validation accuracy of 96.50% with average precision and recall value of 95.9% and 93.3% respectively, while YOLO v7 has validation accuracy of 87.6% with average precision and recall value of 81.9% and 85.4% respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis and Investigation of a Novel Compact Metasurafce Absorber with Wide Angle Stability for Triple Band Attributes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This manuscript is about the analysis and investigation of a novel configuration of metasurface absorber which consists triple square ring with a vertical conducting strip. The key characteristics of the absorber design are examined and fine-tuned to demonstrate the successful individual adaptation of each of the three absorption frequency points. The simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed meta-absorber shows exceptional absorption rates and remains unaffected by polarization across a wide range of incoming wave angles in three frequency bands, for both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) wave modes of operation. The simulated results present that the suggested metabsorber exhibits three absorption peaks at frequencies of $3.5 \mathrm{GHz}, 5.2 \mathrm{GHz}$, and 6.5 GHz, with corresponding absorption values of $94 \%, 91 \%$, and $96 \%$ respectively. The simulation of the proposed model is carried out by HFSS electromagnetic solver.

articleTitle: Frequency Sensitive Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Constant power consumption is a problem in lowpower devices, especially in wearable electronics such as ECG monitors. This issue is targeted in the research article by designing and simulating a frequency-sensitive triggering circuit. The purpose is to make a main circuit operational when an input signal is in a particular frequency band, which is the $0-150 \mathrm{~Hz}$ band. This is done by designing a low pass filter that enables only signals in the required frequency range while blocking other frequencies at the supply of 3.3 V. The filtered signal is then converted from AC to DC using the rectifier circuit, which gives a steady voltage output. A comparator is used to initiate the main circuit by comparing the generated voltage with a reference voltage. The result is a significant decrease in power consumption as the circuit takes only 23.1 $\mu \mathrm{W}$, which is immensely lower than ECG wearable devices having a sleep mode power consumption that ranges up to 3 mW. This is the approach that provides a more efficient solution for the constant monitoring of wearable healthcare devices.

articleTitle: An Effective Customer Segmentation using RFM Ranking Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Customer segmentation emerged as a technique to develop a relationship between customer buying behavior and company profits. With the ever-growing data within the market and the extreme competition among the companies to capture the market, it has become very important for companies to understand the data accumulated by them wisely and efficiently. This can be achieved by customer segmentation techniques. It is directly related to customer relationship management (CRM) system. Therefore, the presented approach aims to provide a research framework to carry out the evolution of different customer segmentation and their behavior. In this paper, the evaluation of the presented approach is evaluated on the online available retail store dataset for one year. The evaluation is carried out using the different approaches such as k-means and k-Medoids algorithm. Further, the segmentation accuracy is gauged by Silhouette distance and mean square error (MSE). The results analyzed through different techniques using the various parameters and show a relationship between customer behavior and marketing strategies of the companies.

articleTitle: A Cost Effective Sustainable Autonomous Unmanned Surface Vehicle for Automated Water Surface Cleaning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This paper presents the IFOR CB-24, a fully automated unmanned surface vehicle (USV) designed for waterbody cleaning and quality testing. Utilizing edge computing, computer vision, and lightweight machine learning algorithms like the Random Forest Classifier, the USV navigates water surfaces, performs quality testing, and removes trash using a custom conveyor belt system. The design focuses on cost-effectiveness, computational efficiency, and environmental sustainability, offering significant advancements in automated waterbody management.

articleTitle: Development of a Chat History Analysis Module Using Advanced Machine Learning Models and Vector Databases for Digital Forensic Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Instant messaging has become a cornerstone of modern communication, playing a significant role not just in daily interactions but also in areas like digital forensics. This paper introduces a Chat History Analysis Module designed to simplify and enhance the analysis of chat datasets from popular messaging platforms. By leveraging advanced machine learning techniques and an efficient vector database, the module can store, search, and retrieve chat messages based on content, sender, receiver, and timestamp.The module was tested using a synthetic dataset of 330 messages, each enriched with metadata such as sender and receiver information, timestamps, and message statuses. It supports multiple languages and generates visualizations that reveal communication patterns, trends over time, app usage preferences, and key relationships between senders and receivers.This solution addresses challenges like handling large volumes of data and multilingual content, bridging the gap between raw chat data and actionable insights. It is a valuable tool for practitioners in the field of digital forensics and aligns with the themes of modeling, simulation, and intelligent computing

articleTitle: Design of Energy Harvesting System using COMSOL Multiphysics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This research demonstrates the increasing need for renewable energy due to environmental concerns and the negative effects of traditional power generation. The goal of the research is to generate electricity using mechanical vibration induced by wind energy. In this research paper, Piezoelectric Macro Fiber Composite (PEH-MFC) system is employed and an innovative technique is proposed by utilizing piezoelectric materials to convert mechanical strain into electricity. For the purpose of designing and simulation, COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2 software is used for modelling the cantilever beam to represent the PEH-MFC system. Wind induced forces and material properties are considered in the design of the energy harvesting system. We will investigate the influence of key parameters such as piezoelectric material selection, the amount of wind-induced force exerted on the substrate to optimise the PEH-MFC system. A parametric study will be conducted to identify the optimal combination of these factors for maximising energy harvesting efficiency. Experimental validation will be performed to verify the simulation results and assess the performance of the system under real-world conditions.

articleTitle: Memristor Emulator Circuit Design using MOCCII
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The development of memristor emulators with particular operating parameters poses a notable challenge, prompting the development of memristor emulator circuits. The design of the memristor emulator introduced in this paper utilizes the Analog Current Mode building block MOCCII (Multi Output Second Generation Current Conveyor), along with a multiplier and a few passive electronic components (two resistors and a capacitor). In comparison with existing memristor emulators based on multipliers, our design distinguishes itself by employing fewer transistors used within the block and operating over a broader frequency range. The proposed memristor emulator demonstrates reliable performance up to a frequency of approximately 40 MHz, exhibiting characteristics akin to those of an ideal memristor. Circuit simulations are conducted using a $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ SCL pdk with a dual power supply of $\pm 1.25 \mathrm{~V}$. The functionality of the proposed circuit is validated by varying the capacitance at different frequencies and adjusting the frequency across various capacitance values. Transient analysis confirms the non-volatile nature of the device.

articleTitle: Investigating The Interplay Between Bare BN Cage and Transition Metal Doped BN Cage with Melphalan Drug
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Utilization of nanoparticles in drug delivery systems may influence patient medication adherence and potentially alleviate severe side effects by targeting the medicine to specific cellular locations. The efficacy of boron nitride nanocages and transition metal-doped (Au) boron nitride nanocages as carriers for the medication melphalan (MIn) in both gaseous and liquid phases was assessed by density functional theory. To comprehend these nanostructures potential for tailored drug administration, we methodically looked at their sensing behaviour through density of state, frontier molecular orbital, ideal adsorption energy, and dipole moment analysis. The measurement of adsorption energy indicated that MIn drug adsorption occurred spontaneously on both bare and doped structures.

articleTitle: Synchronization of Phononic Frequency Combs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Phononic frequency combs constitute an array of equidistant vibrational frequencies. In this paper, we simulated a two-coupled van der Pol-Mathieu model to showcase the synchronization of phononic combs. We charted out the values of various system and drive parameters corresponding to the synchronized state. These results can have implications to phononic comb-based sensing and communications.

articleTitle: Explainable AI in Biometrics: A Novel Framework for Facial Recognition Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In recent years, the integration of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in facial biometrics has gained momentum, driven by a growing need for transparency in automated decision-making systems. This paper explores the application of XAI in face detection and identification to bridge the gap between model accuracy and interpretability, aiming to address challenges unique to biometric systems, including bias mitigation, user trust, and ethical implications. Unlike traditional “black-box” models, the proposed framework incorporates visual and feature-based explanations that highlight key facial regions contributing to identification outcomes, enabling more transparent model assessments. We evaluate the effectiveness of state-of-the-art XAI techniques, such as SHAP, LIME, and Grad-CAM, through rigorous testing on diverse datasets under varying conditions, including occlusions, lighting, and facial expressions. Additionally, this research introduces a novel hybrid interpretability metric tailored to biometric applications, assessing the quality of explanations based on fidelity, usability, and impact on user trust. Results demonstrate that the proposed XAI-enhanced model offers insights into decision processes without compromising accuracy, advancing the state of explainability in biometric systems. This work underscores the importance of explainability as a means to achieve ethical, reliable, and legally compliant AI systems in sensitive domains like facial biometrics.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Power Time-Domain Comparator for High-Speed Analog to Digital Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The comparator is a crucial component of an Analog-to-Digital Converter(ADC). In this work, we developed a power-efficient Time-Domain Comparator(TDC) for high-speed Data Converters. This circuit minimizes static power dissipation by using the Clock(CLK) to control the current-starved type inverter. The circuit operates on the principle of Voltage-to-Time Conversion. The comparator effectively converts the analog input voltage into a time delay, creating a phase difference between the input and reference signals. When the input voltage(VIN) is higher than the reference voltage(VREF), the TDC produces a logic low at the output. If the input voltage(VIN) is lower than the reference voltage(VREF), the TDC produces a logic high at the output. The circuit is designed to operate at a speed of 1GHz with a supply voltage of 1V. It consumes 28uW of power and provides a FOM(figure of merit) of 28.03fJ/Conversion. The dead zone voltage measures 19mV with an average delay of 81pS. This circuit was designed using TSMC 12FF and simulated using Cadence Virtuoso.

articleTitle: Electrothermal Modelling of Drain Current in GaN HEMTs using Artificial Neural Network and Global Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Thermal effect represents one of the main challenges for GaN power transistors. In addition to ambient temperature, the power dissipation-induced self-heating represents the main source of heating. This electrothermal effect must be accounted for by the transistor model to provide reliable circuit design. This paper makes use of a single-hidden layer Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to model the drain current. A recently developed global optimization approach is used to train the model and optimize its weights and biases. The model is applied to $8 \times 125-\mu \text{m}$ and $16 \times 250-\mu \text{m}$ GaN High Electron Mobility Transistors (HEMTs) and compared with measurements. Excellent results obtained validate the effectiveness of the ANN-based modeling and optimization methods of power transistors. The main advantage of the approach is its technology independence; thus, it could be applied to a wide range of microwave power transistors.

articleTitle: Optimal Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy Severity Levels Using Attention-Based CNN and Vision Transformers (ViT)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Diagnosing diabetic retinopathy (DR) from colour fundus images is challenging as it requires skilled clinicians to recognize and interpret multiple small features and utilize a complex grading system, making the process both difficult and time-consuming. Prior detection of this condition is important to prevent any further complications such as partial or complete blindness. This study presents an approach for detecting the severity levels of diabetic retinopathy using a combination of Attention-Based Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Vision Transformers (ViT). The method addresses the need for accurate classification of retinal images across multiple severity levels of diabetic retinopathy. We made use of a unique combination of attention mechanisms in CNN and transformers, thereby enhancing the model's ability to focus on critical regions within the retinal images. Experimental results show improvements in classification accuracy of around $95 \%$, sensitivity, specificity, and other key performance metrics, making it a potentially better solution for automated diabetic retinopathy detection.

articleTitle: Mitigate the cold start problem in Recommendation System based on Matrix Factorization and Similarity Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Recommendation System (RS) is a powerful information filtering artificial intelligence tool, which recommend relevant and authentic information for e-commerce user’s onecommerce platform like amazon, flip cart etc. but lack of availability in the rating or reviews for the new customer and items, complicate the prediction of user’s interest and result is less accurate recommendation that is cause of cold start issue in RS. Therefore, to overcome cold start issue in RS, we proposed sequence set similarity technique along with k-NN, Matrix Factorization(MF) and Singular value decomposition(SVD++) and Non negative Matrix factorization(NMF).The Python platform is used for its implementation, accuracy obtain on both Movielens dataset, ML-100k is $0.9454 \%$ and ML-1M is $0.9711 \%$.In this paper, proposed solution verify and validate performance of RS and addressing cold start issue.

articleTitle: Link strength prediction in global financial networks using optimized BiLSTM models: A case of dynamic cross-market equity networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This study develops a model to forecast crossmarket linkage strengths for global stock market networks using dynamic edge weight graphs and optimized BiLSTM approach. It uses forty-three global market indices data of 14 years duration. The models are trained using historical network structure data over a series of time steps. Additionally, hyper-parameter tuning is performed to optimize performance. The model is validated using nested cross validation and are benchmarked against XGBoost and Deep Neural Network. Optimized models are experimented using multiple sets of network structures (unfiltered, filtered, low edge weighted networks) and optimum training sizes are obtained. Model trained with unfiltered networks demonstrated better relative predictability.

articleTitle: Hybrid ASR for Resource-Constrained Robots: HMM-Deep Learning Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This paper introduces a hybrid Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) system tailored for resource-constrained robots. The approach combines Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) with deep learning models, distributing processing tasks via socket programming. HMM-based processing resides within the robot, while a separate PC runs the deep learning model. The synergy of HMMs and deep learning optimizes speech recognition accuracy. Experiments on diverse robotic platforms demonstrate real-time, precise speech recognition. The system’s adaptability to changing acoustic conditions and compatibility with lowpower hardware highlight its efficacy in environments with computational limitations. This hybrid ASR paradigm presents a promising path for seamless human-robot interaction.In conclusion, this research contributes a pioneering dimension to robotics-oriented ASR techniques. By utilizing socket programming to distribute processing tasks across distinct devices, and strategically employing HMMs and deep learning models, the hybrid ASR system demonstrates its potential in enabling robots to adeptly comprehend and respond to spoken language, even in environments with restricted computational resources. This paradigm presents an innovative trajectory for seamless humanrobot interaction in various real-world contexts.

articleTitle: An Experimental Analysis of Forensics and Deepfakes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The growing popularity of smartphones with high-resolution digital cameras, the development of deep learning AI platforms, and the accessibility of a large selection of software programs for shooting, editing, and sharing photos and videos have all contributed to the emergence of a new phenomenon known as “Deepfake.” In response, we have developed and put into use a deep-fake detection model (DFT-MF) that is centred on mouth features. Our algorithm examines and verifies lip/mouth motions in order to detect Deepfake films using deep learning techniques. Our DFT-MF model performed well in classification, according to experiments conducted on datasets containing both actual and fraudulent videos. This was especially true when compared to other methods that have been used in this domain previously.

articleTitle: Generic Memcapacitor Design with Tunable and Resistorless Features and Experimental Investigations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: A resistorless and electronically tunable memcapacitor (MC) design has been presented as one of the new memory elements due to quick progress in the memory circuit. In order to create the memcapacitor circuit, an operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) was employed as the active current mode building block. The basic characteristic of the MC in the design is a hysteresis loop. The performance evaluation was conducted using the Cadence Virtuoso EDA tool. Simulations were performed with a 180 nm TSMC process and a supply voltage of $\pm 1.2 \mathrm{~V}$, providing strong support for the theoretical analysis. The theoretical proposition is supported by the simulation findings.

articleTitle: Co-operative Clustering in Integrated LEO Satellite and Terrestrial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Integrated LEO (Low Earth Orbit) satellite and terrestrial networks represent a transformative approach to global communication, combining the strengths of both satellite and ground-based systems. This integration is critical as the demand for high-speed, reliable connectivity continues to grow, driven by the proliferation of IoT devices, mobile applications, and the need for global coverage. However, the fusion of these two networks presents a range of technical challenges such as energy conservation, and coordination between different network entities, including user equipment (UE), terrestrial base stations, LEO satellites, spectrum usage, interference etc. This paper proposes a Modified Location Weight-based Clustering Algorithm (MoLoClus) done on both user equipment (UE) and LEO satellites by the terrestrial base station and satellite gateway respectively to ensure cooperative communication among users & satellites as well as among clusters to improve network performance in terms of reconfigurability, adaptability, flexibility, energy conservation efficiency, link stability, and self-organizability.

articleTitle: Automated Plant Disease Detection Using CNNs and YOLOv5: A Comprehensive Approach with Grad-CAM and VGG16
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks will be used in the proposed research project to create a plant disease detection system (CNNs). Object detection is used (Yolov5), so it is the model having (Gradcam and yolov5 with vgg16). The system will be created to analyze digital photos and quickly and effectively detect diseases in plant leaves. With the help of a sizable collection of plant photos, both healthy and diseased plants will be included, and the CNN model will be trained to recognize different diseases. The study will go through various phases, including data gathering, data preprocessing, model construction, and model assessment. To eliminate artifacts and to standardize the photos, the acquired data will be preprocessed. Modern methods will be used in the design of the CNN model, which will then be optimized to attain high disease detection accuracy. By offering an automated and precise technique for identifying plant diseases, the suggested technology has the potential to revolutionize the field of plant disease detection. This may result in prompt treatment and intervention, reducing crop loss and increasing agricultural output. The proposed approach can also decrease the need for manual diagnosis and inspection, saving farmers and researchers time and money on labor. The overall goal of this research project is to support the creation of an effective and trustworthy system for detecting plant diseases that can have a significant impact on the agriculture sector.

articleTitle: Agroprobe: Integrated NPK And Moisture Content Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In this paper an smart device for farmers is been proposed, which is an initiation toward technology in Agriculture. The proposed AGROPROBE focuses on innovating the way soil monitoring is done with the use of a sensor system based on Raspberry Pi Pico W, which can provide necessary details on soil, such as moisture content and NPK (Nitrogen, Phosporous and Potassium) values. The data is uploaded to the thing speak cloud for analysis and prediction using Machine Learning (ML) model. In this paper seven ML model were compared to offer insightful predictions in soil management. The proposed model solves the farmer efforts instead reaching irrigation office, directly using proposed agroprobe, which recommends the suitable crop based on soil type. In this paper black soil samples were tested and crop is been recommended using ML model.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of 3D Printing Defects using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In the realm of Industry 4.0, the adoption of 3D printing has emerged as a transformative force, promising significant cost savings and heightened time efficiency. These products are intricately crafted in a layer-by-layer fashion, guided by digital Computer-Aided Design (CAD) inputs. However, despite these advantages, 3D-printed items encounter challenges from alterations in material properties, variations in printing conditions, and structural complexity, leading to defects that compromise the quality and integrity of the final product. This research introduces an innovative approach to bolstering quality assurance in 3D printing, integrating convolutional neural networks (CNN) and reinforcement learning. Leveraging the powerful image recognition capabilities of CNNs, the study enhances defect detection, identifying flaws often overlooked by traditional inspection methods. Additionally, reinforcement learning allows the system to adapt and improve over time, creating a dynamic tool for quality control. The CNN achieved a final training accuracy of 97.99% and demonstrated robust generalization in the validation set, highlighting its potential for precise defect detection in real-world applications. This approach paves the way for adaptive and self-improving systems in Industry 4.0 manufacturing environments.

articleTitle: Enhancing/Suppressing the Operational Range of Phononic Frequency Combs using Optical Tweezers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Phononic frequency combs (PFC) are typically generated in mechanical resonators through nonlinear interactions of phonon modes. Our previous work derived the existence conditions for modal-coupling mediated PFC generation. This paper presents a route to improve this operational range of PFC using optical tweezers. The force exerted by the optical tweezers on mechanical resonators modulates the dynamics of PFC to either enhance or suppress its operational range.

articleTitle: Plant-Leaf Disease Detection: A Comparative Analysis With Machine Learning and Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Agriculture is vital to human civilization, providing food and economic benefits. However, crops and plant leaves are vulnerable to various illnesses that hinder growth. Early and accurate identification of pathogens can prevent further damage, but current manual methods by farmers could be more efficient and precise, leading to potential crop destruction and reduced yields. Utilizing computerized image processing techniques can minimize losses and boost productivity. Images of affected leaves or crops can be used to identify and classify plant diseases using a variety of techniques. Significant advancements have been made, particularly with deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) techniques, including convolutional neural networks (CNN), which are favored for their ability to process image information and understand spatial hierarchies. Selecting between traditional machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches depends on the nature of the problem, the availability of data, and computational resources. For intricate tasks like image detection and classification, DL—particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs)—is preferred when sufficient data and processing capabilities are accessible.

articleTitle: On the Photothermal Excitation of Phononic Frequency Combs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Ever since the discovery of phononic frequency combs (PFC), the excitation of PFC in microelectromechanical (MEMS) devices has almost always been through electrical driving. Our previous work showcased the possibility of exciting PFC using optical fields via mechanical overtone effects. This paper explores an alternative mechanism of photothermal excitation for PFC generation. An expression has been derived for the threshold laser power $\left(P_{t h}\right)$ required to excite PFC. We studied the influence of various physical parameters of mechanical resonator and laser on $\boldsymbol{P}_{\boldsymbol{t} \boldsymbol{h}}$.

articleTitle: Advances in Mango Leaf Disease Detection Using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In the pursuit of addressing the persistent challenges in agriculture, particularly in the realm of mango cultivation, this research paper marks the culmination of deep learning and computer vision. Focused on the imperative task of mango leaf disease detection, our study introduces innovative advancements, leveraging deep learning models. Our approach embraces a diverse ensemble of deep learning architectures, namely DenseNet121, EfficientNetB2, MobileNetV2, ResNet50, VGG16, and VGG19. Each model is meticulously trained and evaluated on an extensive dataset containing images of healthy and diseased mango leaves. The objective is to develop a robust system capable of accurate and efficient mango leaf disease identification. The results obtained from our experiments are encapsulated in a comprehensive analytics table, showcasing the performance metrics of each model. Notably, ResNet50 exhibits unparalleled accuracy at $\mathbf{9 9. 1 2 \%}$, with impressive precision, recall, and F1-score values. Our research extends beyond model evaluations, delving into the intricate nuances of each algorithm’s contributions. This critical examination serves to guide practitioners and researchers in selecting the most suitable model for their specific agricultural applications. As a testament to the practicality and real-world applicability of our research, we present a robust discussion on the implications of deploying these models in precision agriculture systems. The significance lies not only in the remarkable accuracy achieved but also in the potential for timely intervention and mitigation of economic losses associated with crop damage. It contributes to a profound understanding of the application of deep learning models in the agricultural domain.

articleTitle: Development of an Insect-Inspired Hexapod Robot: Design, Construction, and Operational Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This paper explores the design, construction, and operation of a hexapod robot inspired by insect locomotion, capable of navigating diverse terrains and performing intricate maneuvers. The development process includes mechanical, electrical, and control systems. The robot’s body was modeled using Fusion 360 and 3D printed for cost-effectiveness and ease of modification, allowing rapid prototyping and iterative improvements. Custom PCBs designed with KiCAD reduce wiring complexity and ensure a compact form factor, enhancing the robot’s internal architecture and reliability. The electronics are managed by an Arduino Mega Pro MINI, selected for its compact size and adequate processing power. The robot is programmed using the Arduino IDE, with modified open-source code to meet project requirements, ensuring a robust control system for various tasks. Initial programming focuses on enabling free navigation, essential for basic movements and environmental response. Future enhancements include sophisticated programming for obstacle avoidance and self-adjustment on uneven terrain, increasing adaptability and functionality. The primary objective is reliable free navigation, with subsequent improvements targeting advanced obstacle avoidance and terrain adaptability. Future iterations aim to increase durability by transitioning to an aluminum chassis and optimizing servo housing. This approach not only improves strength but also performance in extreme conditions, demonstrating the potential of 3D printing and custom PCB design for rapid prototyping and optimization in robotics.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuned BERT Model for Accurate Hate Speech Detection in Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Over recent years, the prevalence of hate speech and provocative language on social media platforms has risen sharply, raising significant concerns about their impact on individuals and society at large. Hate speech can inflict harm on both individuals and groups, deepen societal divisions, and even incite violent acts. Therefore, the objective of the paper is to identify and eliminate hate speech from social media to help maintain a respectful and healthy online environment. The proposed work analyzes the BERT Model that has been fine-tuned by utilizing the Hugging Face library, to detect hate speech, offensive language, and neutral content. The aim of the research is to evaluate the model’s accuracy and other performance metrics in identifying hate speech and offensive language. For training and testing, we employ a labeled dataset from Kaggle containing instances of offensive and hateful language. The BERT model uses a pre-trained tokenizer from the Hugging Face Transformers library, specifically the case-sensitive base BERT model, to tokenize and encode text for classification purposes. The model achieves an overall accuracy of ${9 0 \%}$.

articleTitle: Non Invasive Glucose Detection Using Triple-Pole Triangular CSRR Sensor: Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In this study, the authors present the design and validation of a compact microwave biosensor aimed at accurately monitoring blood glucose concentrations in hyperglycemic and hypoglycemic patients. The Triple Pole Triangular Complementary Split-Ring Resonator (TP-TCSRR) sensor, with dimensions of $60 \times 20 \times 0.8 \text{mm}^{3}$, features three triangular complementary split-ring resonators. The sensor is constructed on top of an FR4 substrate, and the bottom layer has a 50 -ohm microstrip line for excitation. The TP-TCSRR was designed and analyzed parametrically using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) software. The validation of the fabricated sensor is carried out using an experimental setup comprising a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA), aqueous glucose solutions (${5 0 - 2 0 0} \mathrm{~ m g} / \text{dL}$), and a container for dispensing the glucose solution. In vitro tests with deionized aqueous glucose solutions ($50-200 \text{mg} / \text{dL}$) showed clear left shifts in the resonant frequency of transmission response, particularly at lower concentrations. To the best of available knowledge, distinct frequency shifts, particularly at lower glucose concentrations such as 50,70, and $90 \text{mg} / \text{dL}$, have not been previously reported. The sensor demonstrated a maximum sensitivity of 859 $\text{kHz} /(\text{mg} / \text{dL})$.

articleTitle: iEEG Based Brain-Computer Interfaces for Neural Encoding of Dynamic Natural Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This research delves into the complex task of interpreting visual stimuli based on intracranial electroencephalogram (iEEG) recordings, leveraging the power of advanced machine learning techniques, specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The study meticulously tackles the challenges encountered in the preprocessing phase of the data and the intricate process required to map the vast iEEG datasets accurately to corresponding visual stimuli. Despite facing these significant hurdles, the research provides profound insights into how brain activity is linked to visual perception. It significantly contributes to the understanding and development of brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and advances the field of neuroscience. By exploring the potential of CNNs to decode visual information from iEEG data, this study not only pushes the boundaries of current technological capabilities but also opens new avenues for exploring the cognitive processes underlying human vision.

articleTitle: Implementation of Microbot to Enhance the Well-being of People working in the Fire Hazards Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: People currently live in a difficult world due to the unpredictable hazards present in a particular area, the explosion in Lebanon, colorado's Cameron peak on fire, Wilfred, alpha and beta hurricanes, the madrid bombings, the Denmark power outrage, etc. The intelligent system must establish and take action to ensure the safety of the public at this point, and plan to accomplish there by introducing an advanced radar system that can be utilized as both a security system and the safest system possible. There are numerous instances where we can use it to protect people and to avoid even worse outcomes, as the ones mentioned above. This scientific study describes the many needs and applications for integrating the radar system with the explosion-proof camera and paga system. The major goal is to investigate a safe and secure security system that will protect medical facilities like hospitals as well as the system of highways and other transportation infrastructure. This ground-breaking security system idea was developed to fully eliminate human mistakes, provide a highly functional system, and increase the availability and efficiency of security systems. This would be possible by combining technologies like cctv, paga, and radar. It can be used for data analysis (transferred over to the cloud), image processing, detection, and protection, Additionally, the micrbot can be used to test the system and analyze the results. The tool, new equipment, and advanced safety purposes are introduced in this study. Whereas a radar system uses an explosion-proof ptz camera to take pictures and a public addressing and general alarm system to warn nearby residents to take safety precautions before something bad happens.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of ZrO2 based ceramic MIMO antenna for smart cities in n257 and n261 Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This article showcases the design of circularly polarized and highly isolated ceramic-based MIMO antenna for millimeter wave application. Modified U shape radiator is used to the excite the ceramic Zr02 radiator. The proposed ceramic loaded design operates in the wide frequency band of 27.5 GHz -34 GHz. The suggested design highlights followings key feature (i) The antiparallel orientation of the antenna provides isolation $\gt45 \mathrm{~dB}$ at 28 GHz (ii) A positive again is achieved throughout the operating band, with maximum gain of 4 dBi. (iii) Generation of fundamental of modes ${\mathrm {HE}}11\delta$ at operating frequencies of 28 GHz leading to the diverse radiation pattern. The consistent radiation characteristics and elevated diversity parameter (ECC, DG and TARC) values of the proposed antenna render it a suitable option for 5G Internet of Things sensing applications.

articleTitle: Efficient Streetlamp Detection with YOLO Models on Edge Device
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This study presents a real-time streetlamp detection system using a Raspberry Pi and dashcam, leveraging YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 models. Tested in various conditions, YOLOv8n outperformed YOLOv5n with a mean Average Precision (mAP) of $73.7 \%$ versus $\mathbf{6 9. 4 \%}$, along with higher Precision and Recall. YOLOv8n demonstrated superior accuracy and reliability, making it better suited for IoT-based smart lighting applications in smart cities. This research underscores the potential of affordable edge-computing for adaptive urban lighting solutions.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Hybrid Renewable Energy System for a Positive Energy Residential Building
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The amalgamation of diverse renewable energy sources to meet building energy demands and achieve sustainable energy goalsis emerging as a significant research focus. This research demonstrates the design and transient simulation of a hybrid renewable energy system, comprising solar panels, a wind turbine, and a battery, to achieve the demands of a Positive Energy Building located in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, utilizing a Trnsys-Matlab simulation framework. An energy routing algorithm is employed to manage energy distribution within the system and extend battery longevity. Our suggested hybrid renewable energy system satisfies the annual energy requirements of the facility while also producing surplus energy for battery charging and storage, hence ensuring optimal battery life.

articleTitle: Considering Power Losses and Voltage Drop in Average-Value Modeling of Voltage Source Inverters in Simulations of AC Machine Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Voltage-source inverters (VSIs) are used extensively in AC machine drive applications. Detailed switching models of VSIs offer accurate but computationally expensive simulations. Average-value models (AVMs) of VSIs are often used for fast and efficient simulations in electromagnetic transient (EMT) programs. However, most conventional AVMs do not consider power losses. This paper extends the previous work on representing the losses in parametric AVMs of VSIs by including the overall losses that are frequency- and current-dependent, as well as voltage drop due to the ON -state resistance of switches. Several new lossy AVMs (LAVMs) and their equivalent circuits are presented. The losses may be implemented on the DC side, AC side, or distributed between the DC and AC sides. The proposed LAVMs are demonstrated on an induction machine drive for which the losses are determined experimentally. The proposed LAVMs exhibit exceptional accuracy in capturing the effects of losses and voltage drop compared to experimental results.

articleTitle: A Simulation-Driven Exploration of Coil Design and WPT System Integration Strategies for High Quality Factor and Reduced Power Reflections
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems have been widely used in autonomous mobile robots. However, the performance of the WPT system is limited due to the low efficiency of the transfer. This research aims to explore the impact of coil design on performance, demonstrating promising improvements in power transfer efficiency and range. Specifically, this research uses high-frequency electrical stimulation to reduce signal reflections in the WPT system. The proposed system, simulated with its three variations and results, shows a significant reduction in signal reflection over a long range compared to previous literature. Furthermore, a derived equation to optimize coil turns improves the quality factor. The results of the proposed system show that using a double-layer coil with intermediate coils is a reliable and effective way to transfer power wirelessly over a long range.

articleTitle: Global Optimization Based Small-Signal Modeling Applied to AlGaN/GaN Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Operating the GaN transistor at high frequencies stimulates additional parasitic effects, which have a strong impact on the RF characteristics of the device. Directly extracting these distributed elements may not be practical, especially for large parameters devices. In this case, an optimization-based approach could be the best alternative. In this paper, different optimization algorithms will be investigated and applied to a small-signal equivalent circuit model. MATLAB codes have been developed and implemented to extract the practical extrinsic elements of a $4 \times 125 \mu \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{GaN}$ on Diamond high electron mobility transistor (HEMT). An extrinsic parameters extraction procedure has been developed based on the Sine-Cosine Algorithm (SCA). The performance of the proposed method was compared with reported optimizations, and the results were very good. The results of this paper are very important for accurate small and large-signal modeling and reliable circuit design.

articleTitle: Application of Residual Neural Network Towards Semiconductor Device Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In this paper, we explore the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in device modeling, focusing on the extraction of electrical characteristic parameters from current-voltage (I-V) curves of Silicon Carbide (SiC) MOSFETs. We trained neural networks with 500 I-V curve images captured from these devices. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first instance where the AI engine has been used to predict threshold voltages from I-V curves of device datasheets. Our study utilized a SiC MOSFET structure in Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) software to generate I-V curves under various mobility and work function parameter variations, resulting in a dataset of 500 different devices’ I-V characteristics. Firstly, we modified the input and output layers of existing ResNet18 model to meet our application. Secondly, we developed a custom six-layer Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for this application, and found improved accuracy and speed. This demonstrates the potential for further improvement and application of ResNet and CNNs in device modeling using images available in the datasheets. Our custom CNN achieved a MSE of 0.05 and an average training time of 22 seconds per epoch, demonstrating significant improvements over the modified ResNet18.

articleTitle: EEG Based Imagined Speech Recognition Using Multi-Feature Extraction with DNN-CapsNet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Classification of EEG-based imagined speech represents a significant advancement in brain-computer interface (BCI) technology. However, current methods often yield lower classification accuracy due to a lack of robust, decodable features. To address this limitation, we propose a hybrid deep learning approach that combines a Deep Neural Network (DNN) and Capsule Neural Network (CapsNet). Our proposed system involves three main stages: signal acquisition, quality assess- ment, and effective feature extraction and classification.First, we conduct a quality assessment of the input EEG signal using conditional entropy. Then, we improve the signal quality through preprocessing, which involves three steps: noise removal, artifact removal, and sampling. Preprocessing is performed using a Hybrid Median Filter and Adaptive Wavelet Packet Denoising Algorithm (HMAPA); artifact removal is handled by Black Widow Optimization (BWO); and sampling is achieved using Cubic Spline Interpolation (CSI). Finally, we extract features and classify the imagined speech signals using the DNN-CapsNet algorithm based on EEG data.The algorithm was implemented using MATLAB R2020a, and its effectiveness was evaluated through various performance metrics. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of classification performance.

articleTitle: VMF: Enhancing Speed Control System of BLDC motor via Estimating the Total Bias based on Variation Model Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Brushless DC (BLDC) motors are widely adopted for their efficiency, precision, and dynamic performance, yet their nonlinear and multivariable dynamics pose significant challenges for conventional control methods. This paper introduces a novel Variation Model Filter (VMF)-based control approach to address these issues. Unlike traditional PID controllers, which struggle with the time-varying nature of BLDC systems, and advanced methods like ADRC that involve high complexity, the proposed VMF technique estimates and compensates for total bias within the system, enhancing robustness and response. Simulation results demonstrate that the VMF-based PID control, also called variation-based control system, outperforms both linear ADRC and conventional PID control in speed regulation and load disturbance rejection. This work presents a robust and simplified solution, offering substantial improvements in BLDC motor control efficiency and cost-effectiveness, with potential for further optimization and practical applications.

articleTitle: Assessing Bias in Large Language Models: A Comparative Study of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become more integrated into various applications, their potential to display and amplify biases is a significant concern. This study evaluates the social and gender bias in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude AI. Unlike previous studies using pre-existing datasets, we used handcrafted questions to reveal biases more effectively. Basic simple questions provided an unbiased answer, however complex biased questions highlighted a few concerns. ChatGPT had a bias all the time while Gemini had a bias sometimes and the rest of the time it did not, or if it did the bias was different, while Claude AI was mostly unbiased. Thus, this study shows that there is variation in levels of bias in different AI models and thus advocates for enhanced strategies of Bias in AI to address the issue of fairness in the use of AI.

articleTitle: Transition from Negative to Positive Parametric Dependence in Phononic Frequency Combs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Phononic frequency combs constitute an array of equidistant vibrational frequencies. In this paper, we simulated a van der Pol-Mathieu model to showcase that the equidistant spacing of phononic combs can be made either positively or negatively sensitive to physical perturbations. These results can have implications to sensing.

articleTitle: Design and Modelling of Integer-N and Fractional-N Frequency Synthesizers using Phononic Frequency Combs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Phononic frequency combs are mechanical vibrations whose spectra are characterized by an array of equidistant frequencies. This paper explores an application of phononic combs towards design and development of integer-N and fractional-N synthesizers. We simulated a van der PolMathieu model to showcase the generation of fractional-N frequencies $\frac{M}{N} f_{{ref }}$ and integer-N frequencies $\frac{1}{N} f_{{ref }}$ at low and high drive amplitudes respectively.

Author Keywords: integer-N frequency synthesizers and fractional-N frequency synthesizers

articleTitle: Neural Net-Eyes: Advanced License Plate Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This paper explores the use of convolution neural networks in detecting and analyzing images into implementing a license plate recognition system. The system utilizes a neural network known as You Only Look Once (YOLO) model for performing border plate recognition around the supplied image and another neural network, Paddle OCR (Optical Character Recognition) for extracting the text within the image. The retrieved number plate is checked against a list of allowed vehicles within the system. The information pertaining to the plate is sent back to users for additional processing from their end.

articleTitle: Hybrid Neural Networks-Analytical Temperature-Dependent Electrothermal Model for GaN Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Operating GaN transistors under high-power conditions leads to significant internal temperature increases that deteriorate device performance. Additionally, the ambient temperature, especially in outdoor environments, introduces further thermal challenges. To ensure reliable circuit design, it is crucial to develop a comprehensive temperature-dependent electrothermal model that accounts for both internal selfheating and external temperature variations. The objective of this paper is to establish such a model by adopting an efficient method that considers these thermal effects. Various optimization techniques were explored to determine the model parameters, and it was found that the combined technique of NN and global optimization could provide an effective modeling alternative especially for large-size and complicated model. The findings of this study are vital for accurate large-signal modeling and designing reliable circuits for high-power applications.

articleTitle: Time of the Day Based Charging of Electric Vehicles along with V2G and Solar Photovoltaic System for Indian Electricity Demand Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The rise in electricity consumption and the energy crisis of fossil fuels has resulted in an upsurge in installing of nondepleting energy. The environmental impacts yielded by the reciprocating engines, along with their lower energy efficiency, have forced returning of the century-old Electric Vehicle (EV) technology. The penetration of EVs into the Indian automobile market and increasing solar installation can cause stress on the grid. The Solar’s peak power generation during the sun hours can be utilized in charging EVs. The technology of Vehicle to Grid(V2G) is employed to utilize the unused charge stored in the EV’s high-capacity kWh-rated battery as the EV remains idle for over 16 hours a day with more than $\mathbf{8 0 \%}$ of the state of charge in it. This paper proposes a framework that integrates solar-based charging of EVs along with V2G. India’s net load demand pattern is studied, and power flow between the grid, solar, and EV is scheduled based on the time of the day is proposed. The validation of the proposed framework is carried out in in MATLAB Simulink for a Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) of 2KW one stage-230V singlephase grid-tied system interfaced with Bidirectional DC-DC (BiDC-DC) and Bidirectional AC-DC (BiAC-DC) power converters and its control strategies.

articleTitle: Analysis of Control Dynamics of a Robotic Arm Using Linear Quadratic Optimal Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Arm robotics is becoming more and more popular due to the need to help humans with difficult and repetitive tasks and the desire to increase productivity. Optimal control techniques are required for better control of robot arms. This paper presents the control dynamics of a two-degree-of-freedom planar robot arm. The non-linear dynamic model of the robot manipulator is linearized using feedback linearization approach followed by Linear Quadratic Optimal Control (LQ Optimal Control) for controlling the robot arm. The control parameters of LQ Optimal control are derived by minimizing a quadratic cost function. Furthermore, a simulation study is presented together with its results to demonstrate the effectiveness of the suggested approach.

articleTitle: Load Management and Allocation of Power in EVs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) provide a sustainable and an environment friendly transportation form. They have superior environmental performance compared to internal combustion engine vehicles especially due to its no atmospheric emission. When charging infrastructure is based on renewable energy sources the ecological advantages of EV adoption are further amplified. In this research a methodology to achieve optimal charging of an EV by integrating State of Charge (SOC) based load management algorithms and power distribution mechanisms is proposed. This work will address the challenges of maintaining a healthy electrical grid amidst growing power demand, particularly due to transportation electrification. Additionally, it also focuses on static power allocation algorithms. Concepts related to dynamically optimize power distribution are explored among system components based on real-time data. Simulation data and experimental validations demonstrate substantial performance and operational range improvements over conventional approaches, emphasizing the potential for advancing the performance of next-generation EVs.

articleTitle: Modified Wheeler Cap Approach for Radiation Efficiency Measurements of On-body RFID Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In this paper, the radiation efficiency of a differentially fed loop antenna is measured using the modified Wheeler Cap (WC) technique. The antenna is matched to the Alien Higgs 9 RFID chip, when placed on a human body-mimicking gel. Characterization of the used gel is first performed, followed by measurements of the wake-up power and impedance of the RFID chip. The WC method using the modified Johnston’s equation published in an earlier work, is applied for radiation efficiency measurements of the proposed loop. Read range measurements are performed for the tag as well, and radiation efficiency is extracted using Friis formula. It is showcased that, for balanced antennas fed by a differential port, and placed over lossy matter giving low overall antenna efficiency, the WC modified method can be applied to measure the radiation efficiency by normalizing the $S 11$ plots to the chip resistance.

articleTitle: Power System Network Modelling to Predict Inter-area Low Frequency Oscillations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This paper highlights the importance of accurately modeling power system network elements and controls using analytical software tools to effectively predict underlying network security issues, particularly under stressed system conditions.While major network events like faults, interconnection trips, bulk load disconnections, and large generating unit trips under normal operating conditions can be analyzed with predictable impacts on system security, occurrences like small signal stability or low frequency oscillations may get overlooked unless highly degraded network states are accurately predicted and modeled in the software. This is especially pertinent for large power systems with multiple nodes, multiple generation sources, and high-impedance interconnectors that create significant electrical distances between power system nodes. Similarly, modelling of accurate controls to be implemented as mitigation measures are crucial to ensure power system security from these undetected issues.This paper presents a case study using power system analysis software tool – Cyme for a large industrial power system network of an Aluminium smelter. The results of the study underscore the importance of precise network element modeling. The results indicate that using simplified data may not be able to highlight the real problems related to inter-area oscillations, while the same could be clearly detected by accurately modeling the systems representing the degraded state of network with tested control parameters. Such accurate modeling assists system operators in avoiding specific operational modes and aids control engineers in deriving optimal control parameters to meet network security requirements. Such accurate prediction of the underlying network issues immensely improves overall Security of Supply (SoS) of an industrial power system.

articleTitle: Enhancing White Blood Cell Detection Using YOLOv8 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: White blood cells (WBCs) play a vital role in the immune system, defending the body against pathogens such as viruses, bacteria, parasites, and fungi, and are produced in bone marrow and lymphoid tissues. Traditional WBC analysis methods rely on manual counting, which is prone to human error and inefficiencies. Recent advancements in computeraided detection systems, powered by deep learning, have significantly improved the accuracy and speed of WBC diagnostics. These systems utilize convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to automatically extract important features from blood smear images, minimizing reliance on manual techniques and enhancing diagnostic reliability. This study employed various YOLO v8 model variants to detect specific WBC types, with evaluation metrics including precision, recall, and mean Average Precision (mAP). The results demonstrates that the YOLOv8 medium and nano variants achieved the highest mAP50 (IoU threshold of 50) value of $\mathbf{9 9 \%}$, while the small variant achieved an mAP50 of $98 \%$ over 25 epochs. When comparing mAP50-95 (IoU threshold of 95), the medium variant attained $91 \%$, while the nano variant achieved $90 \%$. Additionally, the nano and small variants reached the highest average precision of $99 \%$, while the medium and nano variants recorded the highest average recall at $\mathbf{9 8 \%}$.

articleTitle: Impact of Deep Learning Techniques on Deep Fake Image Identification for Digital Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In recent years, deep fakes have become increasingly prevalent and sophisticated, raising concerns about misinformation. This has led to a surge in research on deep fake creation, detection techniques, and related datasets. The best approaches for detecting deep fakes often involve deep learning techniques, primarily using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). This article proposes a deep learning-based method using CNNs to identify deep fake videos by analyzing frame-level inconsistencies that generative models struggle to replicate. Our approach combines multiple convolutional layers to capture spatial hierarchies and detect subtle visual cues that differentiate real from fake content. The proposed model demonstrates strong performance, achieving high detection accuracy and robustness across several deep fake generation methods. Extensive testing on public deep fake datasets shows that CNN-based models are effective tools for automated deep fake detection, offering a promising countermeasure to the growing misinformation problem. In Deep Fake and Real image (Dataset1) and Bigger Dataset for Image Deepfake Detection (Dataset2), these two dataset we used to detect the real and fake images and the highest accuracy of dataset-1 using CNN model is 96.28% among all the models and in the dataset-2 the highest accuracy was 68.02% by using the Xception model. Following that, we built and trained our model with the maximum accuracy at an acceptance rate of 96.2% using CNN,NN, Xception, DenseNet-121, and EfficientNetB0.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for a 2-DOF Robotic Arm: Dynamics and Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The growing interest in arm robotics is driven by the need to facilitate complex and repetitive jobs for humans, as well as by the advancement of production. There is a need for optimal control techniques for better control of robot arms. This paper presents the control dynamics of a planar robot arm with two degrees of freedom using the Model Predictive Control (MPC) technique. It uses the feedback linearization technique to linearize the nonlinear control dynamics of the robot manipulator. The control parameters using the model predictive control technique are achieved by minimizing a quadratic criterion. Furthermore, a simulation analysis and its results are outlined to emphasize the efficiency of the presented technique.

articleTitle: Examining The Performance of Sense Amplifiers for In-Memory Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The principle of in-memory computing offers a highly promising framework that may effectively tackle the discrepancy between memory and computing, leading to exceptionally fast and energy-efficient data processing. The sense amplifier serves a vital role in the realm of in-memory computer architectures. The effectiveness and energy efficiency of in-memory computing systems are heavily reliant on the suitability of their sense amplifiers. This paper offers a comprehensive insight into the main goal of pinpointing sense amplifiers designed specifically for in-memory computing applications. It involves an examination of the requisites and inherent challenges linked to in-memory computing. This encompasses various factors, such as delay, energy efficiency, and resilience to process changes. A careful examination was conducted to analyze the intricate trade-offs associated with power consumption, energy efficiency, and processing speed. The considerations play a pivotal function in providing designers with the essential knowledge and confidence to proficiently include sense amplifiers into diverse in-memory computing systems. This paper presents a systematic approach to selecting and constructing sense amplifiers to enhance our understanding of in-memory computing. We tailor our approach to match the distinct requirements of different inmemory computing applications. The results gained are anticipated to have a substantial influence on the progression of memory-centric computing systems in the forthcoming years.

articleTitle: Analog CMOS Implementation of Margin Propagation Algorithm Using Switched Capacitor Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
