abstract: The margin propagation (MP) technique is implemented uniquely in this study by utilizing switched capacitor circuits to transfer charge. Employing charge conservation to achieve the reverse water-filling principle, the MP algorithm, well-known for its effective piecewise linear approximation to the log-sum-exp function, is used in this application. The reverse water-filling process is efficiently followed by the suggested circuit designed using CMOS 180 nm Technology, as shown by simulation results, which yield desirable outcomes. Furthermore, an exhaustive assessment of the circuit’s correctness confirms its effectiveness in real-world uses, which advances the field of circuit design for efficient algorithmic approximation.

articleTitle: Effect of Inclined Magnetic Field on Stokes Flow Through In-Phase Slip-Patterned Microchannel Using Boundary Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: An investigation is conducted on a twodimensional hydrodynamic model of pressure-driven, viscous, incompressible steady creeping flow through a rectangular microchannel that features wall roughness and is influenced by an external inclined magnetic field. The Stokes equations, incorporating the Lorentz force term, are numerically solved using the boundary element method. The wall roughness is mathematically modeled using alternate Navier’s slip and noslip boundary conditions on the surfaces. We investigated streamline contour plots, flow profiles, shear stresses, and pressure gradients for varying the assumed dimensionless parameters to get a complete comprehension of fluid physics. The proposed study has various significant implementations, including regulating and enhancing the mixing and thermal removal inside micro-scaled devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Urban Water Distribution: The Role of Automated Systems and PLC Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Due to the increase in population accompanied by the expansive growth of urban residential areas, the demand for efficient and reliable water distribution systems has increased rapidly. And as urbanisation increases day by day this demand for water is equal to the need for sustainable water management and distribution systems. Thus, it becomes an utmost necessity for the implementation of proper controlling and monitoring mechanisms to prevent wastage of water and also attempts of water theft. As a solution to these challenges, many advanced technologies have been identified all over the world to ensure effective distribution of water to reach every household especially in urban areas. Therefore, my paper estimates and understands the current state of automated water distribution systems with a prime focus on monitoring performance and control through PLC (programmable logic controller) applications. In the initial areas of this paper, it focuses on the basic concept of automatic water distribution that has been implemented in the current scenario in urban areas. This study includes thorough research on the details of the system, how it is operated, its principles, and intended functions. The next stage of research will be focussed on a comparative analysis of various technologies that have been studied and implemented in the field of automated water distribution. This paper shows key innovations, challenges and future goals in the realm of automated water distribution. It also shows the possibility for the integration of PLC systems, discussing how efficiently these systems contribute to the optimization of the water distribution process. Thus, proving PLC systems plays a crucial role in improving the overall performance and sustainability of water distribution systems by monitoring real-time data.

articleTitle: Adaptive Multi-metric Geographic Routing Protocol for FANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Flying Ad-Hoc Networks (FANETs) have gained remarkable importance across diverse industries. Critical applications such as disaster response, reconnaissance, and emergency assistance rely on efficient data delivery within FANETs. However, designing a robust routing protocol for FANETs is challenging because of their distinct characteristics, including high mobility, varying topology, sparse connectivity, and fluctuating link qualities. This study addresses these challenges by proposing an adaptive multi-metric geographic routing (AMGR) protocol. AMGR aims to establish a robust routing path by considering multiple metrics such as link quality, connectivity, and progress. Using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), AMGR dynamically prioritizes these metrics, enhancing its adaptability to dynamic network conditions. The effectiveness of AMGR is evaluated through simulations using ns-3 and compared with two existing geographic routing protocols: Greedy Perimeter Stateless Routing (GPSR) and Utility Function based Greedy Perimeter Stateless Routing (UF-GPSR). Simulation results show that AMGR achieves a better packet delivery ratio and end-to-end delay than GPSR and UF-GPSR.

articleTitle: MediClass-RF: An Optimized Random Forest Framework for Medicinal Plant Classification with Feature Importance and Comprehensive Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Proper categorization of medicinal and non-medicinal herbs is essential for further application in healthcare and the herbal industries. In our work, we proposed MediClass-RF, the Random Forest-based optimized framework aimed at medicinal plant classification, providing feature importance analysis and in-depth performance metrics evaluation. MediClass-RF was trained on a dataset that contains instances of real-world medicinal plants and non-medicinal plants. The popular term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency approach fed these plants' properties into the modules, and synthetic ones with labels of different quality were added artificially to control noise levels and, therefore, simulate practical usage more accurately. These plants' properties were fed into the model using a popular approach. The Random Forest model was trained, tested, and validated with the normal 70:30 separation of training and testing sets, and it performed well, scoring $89 \%$ overall accuracy. In terminologies of performance, the model had a recall of 0.71, indicating its capability to capture a significant portion of actual medicinal plants, and an $F 1$-score of 0.83, signifying stability among precision with recall. According to the feature importance study, the most important features leading to classification are terms with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antibacterial activities. Furthermore, an Area Under the Curve (AUC) suggests the model's great power in recognizing medicinal properties against non-medicinal plants. Cross-validation was done five times to validate the model further, obtaining a mean accuracy score of 0.88, calculated out of $0.875,0.91666667$, $0.875,0.83333333,0.91666667$, demonstrating the model's robustness across diverse subsets of the data. This work shows the possibility of machine learning, specifically Random Forest, in medicinal plant classification, making it a valuable tool for medicinal plant specialists and investigators.

articleTitle: Improving the search for information from Kazakh-language content in search systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The presented paper is devoted to exploring the ways to enhance the possibility of finding Kazakh-language text in search engines and improve the quality of search results. There have not been many studies conducted on data retrieval in the Kazakh language, and major search engines do not prioritize processing languages with small audiences, such as Kazakh. During the study, an analysis was conducted on the search results for Kazakh-language data in two search engines frequently used in Kazakhstan: google.kz and yandex.ru. The analysis revealed that these search engines are unable to sufficiently process textual data in Kazakh. To address this issue, the study proposed utilizing morphological analysis and identifying basic forms of searching words. Further, a test search engine was developed taking into account the identified shortcomings, and its results were compared with the results of other search engines.

articleTitle: Nucleotide Feature Extraction Using Fuzzy Triangular Numbers for Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Cancer is one of the world’s major causes of death. In cancer cells, several macromolecules are changed compared to normal cells, including the DNA sequence. In this study, features are extracted and selected using a fuzzy-based nucleotide distribution, and cancer is diagnosed using a machine-learning classification technique. We specifically analyze these nucleotide characteristics in both cancer and noncancer DNA sequences. We tested several cancer classifications approaches, including support vector machines (svm) with various kernel functions, decision trees, and random forests. Fuzzy-based feature extraction uses fuzzy features to estimate the nucleotide probability distribution, demonstrating its potential to reduce processing costs and feature complexity. This technique’s efficacy has been thoroughly evaluated using large-scale case studies, 5 -fold cross-validation, and accuracy testing. Cancer prediction increases dramatically when the classifier and feature reduction approaches used in fuzzy-based feature extraction are explicitly linked. We use genomic locations to differentiate between cancerous and non-cancerous DNA sequences. SVM-linear and SVM-Radial Basis Function (RBF) obtained 100% identification rates for cancerous and non-cancerous DNA sequences, but Decision Tree and Random Forest outperformed SVM with sigmoid and polynomial kernels.

articleTitle: Soft Actor-Critic Algorithm in High-Dimensional Continuous Control Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In this study, we implement and evaluate the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm to address high-dimensional continuous control tasks in simulated environments. SAC, an off-policy deep reinforcement learning algorithm, is known for its sample efficiency and stability due to its maximum entropy objective, which encourages exploration by maximizing both reward and action entropy. This research focuses on applying SAC to the challenging Ant-v4 environment from the OpenAI Gym libraries. These tasks, with their complex state-action spaces, provide an ideal setting for evaluating the robustness and performance of SAC. Our experiments investigate the impact of key hyperparameters, such as the entropy weight ($\alpha$), learning rate, and reward scaling, on training stability and efficiency. Results demonstrate SAC’s ability to achieve competitive performance with improved exploration but highlight its sensitivity to hyperparameter settings, particularly the reward scale and entropy weight. We found that SAC outperformed baseline methods on complex tasks when optimally tuned but required precise adjustments for stable learning. This work provides insights into the practical implementation of SAC in continuous control applications, identifying challenges and proposing adjustments to enhance stability. The findings underscore SAC’s effectiveness in complex environments, with the potential for further refinement in hyperparameter tuning and adaptive entropy regulation.

articleTitle: Aqua Optimize Transformation of Water Management With Cloud-Powered Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Effective water quality monitoring is crucial to ensuring the sustainability and safety of water resources, particularly in fields such as municipal water management, aquaculture, and agriculture. Traditional methods often result in water wastage, environmental degradation, and public health risks due to delayed responses and manual inefficiencies. With the rising focus on sustainable resource management and the impacts of climate change, there is a pressing need for innovative solutions that enable real-time water quality assessment. This research presents an Internet of Things (IoT)-based water quality monitoring system that connects multiple sensors to cloud-based platforms for continuous data analysis. The system monitors key parameters—temperature, flow rate, pH, and water depth—and transmits data using the MQTT protocol to visualization tools like Grafana and Power BI. These tools provide stakeholders with interactive dashboards, displaying real-time water quality trends, anomalies, and alerts for immediate action. The system recommends scalability to adapt a range of industrial applications, providing a cost-effective solution for both small and large-scale water management needs, based on its modularity. Compared to traditional methods, the proposed system improves water quality assessment accuracy, reducing human error and manual inefficiencies by over 30%. Cloud-based data storage and visualization reduce processing times by 40%, while the automated alert system accelerates response times by 25%, allowing prompt interventions when water quality falls below critical thresholds. The system’s adaptable, modular architecture allows for seamless integration with existing water management frameworks in urban water distribution, wastewater treatment, and agriculture. This research demonstrates the system’s potential to enhance water resource management, lower operational costs, and promote environmental sustainability across diverse sectors.

articleTitle: Data Visualization for CTI: A Peek into the Venus Marketplace of the Dark Web
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Dark web is the hidden region of the Internet. The anonymity it offers is of course used for rightful causes such as free speech; but it also brings in users that use it for illicit activities. The latter forms the basis for implementing and leveraging cyber threat intelligence. This work commences with an extensive literature review on the dark web. Building on this foundation, the work initially crawls for dark web market links using a safety net over a VPN. From the links that are gathered the Venus marketplace is shortlisted for data extraction and analysis. A crawler extracts data on all products and vendors in this market, by making use of anti-detection techniques. Through exploratory data analysis, visual representations of the collected data are generated offering valuable insights into the marketplace. Key findings include the most prominent product categories, average prices per category, distribution of products, total sales per vendor, and identification of the top five vendors present in the marketplace. These insights provided a thorough understanding of the Venus marketplace, its products, and its vendors which could be used for cyber threat intelligence.

articleTitle: LoRaWAN and Biosensor-Assisted Smart City Framework to Mitigate the Effects of Lung Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Urbanization and industrialization in cities present substantial obstacles to air quality, resulting in detrimental effects on public health, including respiratory health. This research introduces an Internet of Things (IoT) framework for a smart city environment using LoRaWAN and sensor networks. The framework utilizes the ESP32 LoRaWAN module to provide real-time monitoring of essential air quality metrics, such as carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), ozone (O3), temperature, and humidity. Integrating biosensors enhances accuracy by identifying distinct biological indicators linked to respiratory well-being. The proposed work aims to use the framework in an urban setting within a global context, demonstrating its capacity to reduce the effects of lung disorders. The ESP32 LoRaWAN module enables effective communication within the sensor network up to 20 kilometers, guaranteeing a robust and adaptable solution for smart city applications. The developed framework provides a scalable and novel method for developing healthier and more sustainable cities, decreasing respiratory disorders as urban settings develop.

articleTitle: Quantum-chemical characterization of binary molecular clusters formed by isopropyl cyanide in interstellar space
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The recent detection of isopropyl cyanide (i-PrCN) in the giant molecular clouds of interstellar space stands as a significant breakthrough in astrochemical and bio-chemical research. The branched carbon structure of i-PrCN, a first-of-its-kind in interstellar detection, is crucial for the formation of molecules essential to life, including amino acids that constitute proteins. Hydrogen bonding interactions between organic molecules also play important role in many chemical and biochemical processes vital for life’s maintenance. In this work, we have investigated the intermolecular hydrogen bonding interactions occurring within the binary clusters formed by iPrCN with other interstellar molecules such as methanol, hydroxylamine and water under the cold temperatures of interstellar space. Detailed and systematic quantum-chemical Density Functional Theory calculations have been performed, and the structural, energetic, electrical, and spectroscopic properties of the clusters have been analysed to gain insight into the formation and stability of molecular clusters in the frigid interstellar environments.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Approach to Dataset Creation for Sentiment Analysis in Malayalam
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Sentiment analysis task provides the unique challenge of analyzing a fraction of human emotion from text, Malayalam which is already a computationally complex language due to its high morphological features and agglutination further enhances these challenges. A dataset of 22,449 samples was prepared from surveys and social media that have been classified as positive, negative, or neutral. To study the applicability of the dataset a Machine learning-based sentiment analysis was carried out. TF-IDF was used for word vectorization and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel and a Random Forest classifier was used. With an accuracy of $85.07 \%$, the RF classifier outperformed the SVM model, which only managed $59.9 \%$. The study outlines potential improvement by expanding the dataset to better represent the low-resource language of Malayalam.

articleTitle: CO2 Emission Prediction in the Cement Industry Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The cement industry, with its clinker production, is one of the largest $\mathrm{C O}_{\mathrm{2}}$ emitters, and continuous efforts are being made to reduce these emissions while enhancing efficiency. Traditional empirical models for predicting CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions often involve numerous assumptions and substantial manual input, leading to potential inaccuracies. This study explores the use of machine learning models to predict Kiln Stack CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Flow Rate based on data from a Clinkerization production line in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE. The 22 input parameters were analyzed using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models to predict emissions more accurately. Model performance was assessed using Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Coefficient of Determination ($\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{2}}$). The Random Forest and Gradient Boosting models yielded the best results, with ${\mathrm {R}}^{2}$ values of 0.984, RMSE values of 6392.97 and 6351.99, and MAE values of 4477.44 and 4495.18, respectively. Kiln feed rate emerged as the most significant factor affecting CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. Future work could integrate these models with sensors for real-time tracking and process optimization to minimize emissions while enhancing clinker production.

articleTitle: Ensemble Machine Learning Based Heart Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Heart disease (HD) poses a significant global health concern, potentially impacting a large portion of the population worldwide. Early detection of heart conditions is crucial for effective treatment. With the prevalence of heart disease on the rise, there's a pressing need for the development of a more efficient detection system. Smoking status serves as a determinant for the presence or absence of disorder in patients. The cardiac disease system aims to identify high-risk patients and key cardiovascular health variables and construct a user-friendly model for easy differentiation between them. Utilizing an ensemble of Machine Learning algorithms, such as K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine, this study focuses on building a robust ensemble machine learning model to improve heart condition diagnosis accurately. The ensemble model, which combines the predictions of these individual classifiers, achieved the highest accuracy of $87 \%$, surpassing the previous highest accuracy of ${8 4 \%}$ obtained from particular models. Various techniques are applied and compared based on age, chest pain, blood pressure (BP), sex, cholesterol levels, and heartbeat, resulting in improved outcomes.

articleTitle: Quadrotor UAV Kinematics and Dynamics: A Comprehensive Model with Suggested Control Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This paper offers a comprehensive and systematic approach to developing the mathematical model for quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), focusing on both kinematics and dynamics. Using the well-established Newton-Euler method, the paper simplifies the modeling process to provide a technically sound yet accessible framework that can be applied across various flight modes. Unlike many previous studies that concentrate on specific flight conditions or control systems, this work focuses purely on presenting a complete guide to deriving the quadrotor model, making it a valuable reference for researchers and engineers looking to understand quadrotor behavior in a detailed and structured manner. Although this paper does not propose or implement new control systems, it suggests a few relevant control strategies that could be used with the provided model, considering the complex dynamics of quadrotors. These strategies serve as a foundation for future research in control system development, highlighting the model’s utility as a key tool in advancing UAV technology. This work fills a gap in existing literature by offering a thorough and practical guide to quadrotor modeling, which is essential for both theoretical study and real-world applications.

Author Keywords: Kinematics and Dynamics of Quadrotor drone

articleTitle: Revamped Lane detection in hazy environments using Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In today’s world of rapidly growing technological markets, image processing has become vital for systems to work on visual data. A noteworthy task would be lane detection in autonomous vehicles. A good lane detection system should be able to perform the processing irrespective of the environment and this mandates that adequate preprocessing should be done. One such preprocessing step is image dehazing. Dehazing is particularly tricky with a heavily hazed image where the background object’s visibility is less than zero. To address this issue, methods like the Atmospheric Scattering Model (ASM) have been constructed to dehaze the image. However, these methods tend to lose the color details of the image. The Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) has recently emerged as a tool for image generation, showing promise in addressing this issue. This research work aims to build a hybrid model by combining the DDPM and ASM approaches named RevampedDehazingDDPM (RD-DDPM). The proposed model recreates the original image while maintaining the visual details to the plausible limit. The proposed model produced PNSR score of 38.59 dB, SSIM score of 0.0989 and LPIPS score of 0.0040 which showcases the outstanding performance of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Cloud Based Soil Nutrient Prediction System for Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Decreasing arable acreage and a growing world population are pushing for new farming systems. Achieving high crop production requires maintaining a balanced nutrient level in the soil. This study offers a machine learning-based model that will predict the NPK fertilizer to achieve the higher crop yields. Field sensor data along with meteorological data and remote sensing data from various test fields are integrated. A random forest and decision tree machine learning model are applied to the integrated data to develop a software tool for precision agriculture, enabling accurate estimation of nutrient requirements. A mobile application is used to share the nutrient prediction with farmers, enabling them to make well-informed choices regarding resource utilization efficiency and environmental friendliness. This research can transform agricultural practices globally and contribute towards food security on earth.

articleTitle: A Critical Review of Mobile Applications in Transportation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This study is a critical review of mobile applications pertaining to transportation. Transportation types considered range from pedestrians to cyclists to cars to trains. The wide range features of mobile applications are presented. The features are often location specific. Often surveys, interviews and technology review precedes design of app. Apps are commonly evaluated through surveys and economic indicators. Machine learning, natural language processing, and deep learning are being used to enhance the app features and functionality.

articleTitle: Efficient Deep Network Architecture for COVID-19 Detection from Computed Tomography Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The globally devastating consequence of COVID-19 or Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome-Coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) has posed immense threat to the life of living beings. Doctors and scientists throughout the world are working day and night to combat the proliferation or transmission of this deadly disease through advances in terms of technology, finances, data repositories, protective equipment, and many other services. Rapid and efficient detection of COVID-19 reduces the rate of spreading this deadly disease and early treatment improve the recovery rate. In this paper, we proposed a new framework to exploit powerful features extracted from the autoencoder and Gray Level Co-occurence Matrix (GLCM), combined with random forest algorithm for the efficient and fast detection of COVID-19 using computed tomographic images. The model’s performance is evident from its 97.78% accuracy, 96.78% recall, and 98.77% specificity.

articleTitle: Ensemble Transfer Learning for Accurate Malaria Detection with Stage Classification & Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Malaria is a mosquito-borne disease caused by the Plasmodium parasite and spreads amongst humans by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquitoes. Conventional detection of the disease relies on examining the travel history of the patient to malaria endemic countries, later blood smears are analyzed under a microscope to detect the presence of malaria. This diagnostic approach requires specialized expertise, a resource often scarce in malaria burdened countries. This paper proposes a novel method to address these issues, to not only classify the presence of malarial infection but also identify the current stage of the malarial infection based on available blood smears. The proposed methodology employs deep transfer learning from multiple pre-trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (VGG16, VGG19, MobileNetV2, Xception, InceptionV3 and a custom trained model). To provide an accurate representation of the best performing models the models have been given weights and the classification is done through majority voting for the classes. This method provides a tested solution for datasets that are unbalanced and for models that are unable to fit the dataset with high accuracy. To also understand how the model can make this prediction it uses Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) to understand which parts of the image are important for the image classification. This method has resulted in a higher overall accuracy and reduced false negative rate. The model has provided a method to help malaria diagnosis and potentially aid in disease control and management.

articleTitle: Graph-Theoretic Distributed Approach for Cyber Contingency Impact Assessment in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The rapid integration of digital technologies into power grids has transformed traditional grids into smart grids, increasing interdependence between cyber and physical components. This interconnection introduces vulnerabilities, where cyber disturbances can significantly impact the operation and stability of the power system. Consequently, evaluating, ranking, and prioritizing cyber contingencies is crucial for maintaining grid reliability and resilience. A novel approach for quantifying cyber contingencies is presented, utilizing the distributed Cyber-Dependent Optimal Power Flow (CDOPF) problem. A graph-theoretic framework models the cyberphysical smart grid, eliminating the need for complex and computationally expensive cyber-physical co-simulations. Nonconvex constraints are convexified using a DC power flow relaxation, enabling more efficient solutions. The distributed algorithms are incorporated using RIAPS (Resilient Information Architecture Platform for Smart Grid), an opensource platform designed to enhance the dependability, resilience, and performance of distributed systems within the smart grid. RIAPS provides a robust framework for decentralized control, fault tolerance, and real-time monitoring, which is crucial for ensuring the resilience of cyber-physical systems in dynamic, distributed environments. The platform supports scalable and efficient integration of distributed algorithms across the grid’s infrastructure, enabling fast decision-making and enhanced grid security. The method is tested on the IEEE 39-bus system with varying partition sizes, demonstrating that the distributed approach outperforms centralized methods in scalability and accuracy. It effectively ranks cyber contingencies and measures their impact on overall grid stability, improving grid security and decision-making capabilities.

Author Keywords: Distributed Cyber-Dependent Optimal Power Flow Problem

articleTitle: Clear Text Visibility: A CNN-LSTM Approach for Frame of Interest Identification in Book Flipping Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Book flipping videos present a distinctive challenge for information extraction, requiring the identification of frames with clear text visibility during dynamic page turns. This paper introduces a novel approach to frame classification in book flipping videos, leveraging the combined effect of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTMs). In particular, a CNN-LSTM model is employed, where a pre-trained CNN captures spatial features, and LSTMs extend the model’s capability to distinguish temporal dependencies critical for page turn detection. Unlike conventional methods, this approach processes entire video sequences, enabling the model to learn intricate Frame of Interest (FoI) detection features indicative of page turns and text visibility. The proposed model offers improved interpretability, effectively classifying frames without compromising transparency. The research opens avenues for automated book digitization, digital library creation, and educational technology applications, enhancing information extraction and reliability from book flipping videos.

articleTitle: Analysing Calcium Distribution in Astrocyte: The Role of Proteins and ER Using Fuzzy Laplace Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The calcium ions that are unbound are very essential for Astrocyte signaling. The calcium ions that are unbound, sometimes known as the second messenger, is crucial for brain communication. A number of astrocyte-related factors affect the amount of free calcium in the cytosol level includes proteins, the endoplasmic reticulum, and the diffusion coefficient, among others. The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) acts like a calcium bank inside the cell, storing a large amount of these important signaling molecules. In this study, we examined the impact of these variables on the concentration of calcium in the cytosol. A reaction diffusion is developed under fuzzy environment. A fuzzy boundary value mathematical model is utilized to study the effect of ER and protein fluxes on unbound calcium ions in astrocytes. Also, using triangular fuzzy numbers, we used the Fuzzy Laplace Transform (FLT) to solve the variable coefficient Fuzzy Differential Equation (FDE). The FLT method is employed to obtain the solution. The obtained results are represented graphically with the help of MATLAB. The effect of protein and ER is found significant. Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s is also associated with abnormalities in the regulation of components like endoplasmic reticulum, and proteins.

articleTitle: Enhancements in Active Cell Balancing and Integration of Protective Systems for Electric Vehicle Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are currently the predominant energy source and energy storage utilized in residential applications, renewable energy sectors, and electric vehicles (EVs). Lithium-ion batteries are susceptible to damage and can ignite if not correctly managed, especially when exposed to elevated temperatures. The importance of battery health in electric vehicles (EVs) cannot be overstated. The battery’s state and health have significantly affected the vehicle’s appearance, performance, and total lifespan. Battery testing, management, and protection are crucial for assuring the safe and reliable operation of batteries without compromising their performance. This paper introduces an enhanced version of the Battery Management System (BMS) that incorporates cell balancing and thermal management techniques to achieve optimal performance and provide the highest level of protection for the product. It is recommended to utilize inductive-based active cell balancing to enhance battery performance in electric vehicles. Furthermore, safeguards have been implemented to prevent damage from excessive heat, voltage, and current throughout the battery’s charging and discharging processes. The test results indicate that the MATLAB Simulink algorithm created is superior to the conventional technique.

articleTitle: Advancing Emotion Detection through Dual-Channel EEG and Peripheral Physiological Signal Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Wearable devices often struggle to capture the full range of emotions accurately through peripheral physiological signals like Electrodermal Activity (EDA), Photoplethysmogram (PPG), and Electromyogram (EMG), leading to reduced classification accuracy. While Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are recognized for their superior emotion detection capabilities, past EEG-based studies have been confined to lab settings with high-end systems using 32-64 channels. There is a growing need for systems that can continuously monitor emotions outside the lab. Modern wearable EEG devices, with configurations from single to eight channels, offer a solution. Our study investigates if integrating EEG data from only two channels in commercial wearable EEG devices with peripheral signals can enhance emotion detection accuracy. Using the publicly available DEAP dataset, which provides EEG and peripheral signals from 32 participants exposed to emotional stimuli, we explore various preprocessing and feature extraction techniques for multimodal emotion detection. The DEAP dataset categorizes emotions based on valence and arousal ratings, converting them into binary class problems: High Valence vs. Low Valence and High Arousal vs. Low Arousal. Intra-class emotion classification is performed using a Random Forest classifier with $\mathbf{5}$-fold cross-validation. Results show that while single-modality peripheral signals achieve classification accuracies of 76-85%, the addition of EEG data significantly boosts accuracy up to $\mathbf{9 5 \%}$. Combining EEG data with peripheral signals also greatly improves individual subject valence and arousal classification accuracy and F1 scores.

articleTitle: Enhanced Corrosion Detection Using YOLO-Based Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Corrosion is a persistent issue for maintenance teams across industries. Any corrosion left undetected can cause significant damage to infrastructure, equipment and machinery posing a threat to the safety of the workers and crews leading to substantial repairs. Standard corrosion detection methods relying on manual inspection by workers are found to be insufficient, being slow and often overlooking early signs of corrosion that could help in prevention. In this study, a comparative analysis of existing system and YOLO based corrosion detection systems is conducted. Our analysis will focus on various performance metrics, assessing each model. The study aims to highlight their key strengths and ability to detect corrosion in images, selecting the best performing model. The evaluation employed precision, recall, F1-score and mAPs, revealing that the YOLO family exhibited rapid and precise outcomes compared to the existing models, with YOLOv9 attaining the most balanced performance with a precision of 0.634.

articleTitle: Predicting Land Cover Changes with Convolutional LSTM Networks: A Case Study of Chatham, Massachusetts
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Land use and land cover changes has become crucial for natural resource management and monitoring, particularly in urban planning. Remote sensing and geographical information systems analyze the changes in land use and land cover, promoting sustainability. Remote sensing images are the major data sources for land cover classification. High spatial resolution images enable more precise analysis and identification of land cover data types. However, better spatial resolution creates new challenges to the existing classification and prediction methods. This research work outlines a new model that integrates the Convolutional Neural Networks and Long Short-Term Memory network model for the prediction of dynamic changes in land cover patterns from historic satellite images. The proposed model is constructed for Chatham, Massachusetts, prediction from Google Earth timelapse imagery taken over 39 years to compile a sequence of 39 annual satellite images. The images are preprocessed to $256 \times 256$ pixels and image normalization ensured efficient data handling. The proposed model predicted land cover over the next three years and demonstrated the model’s capacity to capture both geographical and temporal patterns in the data. Evaluation of metrics, such as the training and validation loss, showed good performance by the model. Despite some limitations in image resolution and iterative prediction, the findings show that CNN-LSTM models could be very useful for land cover forecasting, providing important guidelines for future study and practical applications in the context of environmental management.

articleTitle: A Simple Piezoelectric Structural Health Monitoring System for use in concrete applications in Real-Time
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This study outlines the creation of a piezoelectric sensor-based system for real-time building monitoring. The sensors convert mechanical vibrations and stresses in the building structure into electrical impulses using the piezoelectric effect. Signal processing is used to discover abnormalities and structural defects in these signals. Their noise floor should be almost zero and their sensitivity high. The proposed technology monitors the building structure instantly, allowing early detection of problems and prompt repairs. Laboratory and outdoor studies prove the approach can effectively detect and pinpoint construction faults. This project aims to create a piezoelectric sensor-based structural health monitoring (SHM) system. Empirical testing showed that these sensors had great sensitivity, low noise, and good sensor resolution. Indeed, they outperform commercial equipment.

articleTitle: Analysis of Historical Weather of Karnataka, India for Insights in Climate Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Climate change in simpler words means the change in the long-term average weather parameters. Climate change is an important issue because its causing imbalance in the environment and affects the lives of all flora and fauna. The climate change is due to many factors, but the major factor is the human activities which are leading to global warming over the past decades. Numerous studies consider analysis of continental or global data, providing the overall insights in climatic changes continentally or globally respectively. The approach in this paper considers regional analysis to provide better insights to the local people needs so they get adapted to the changes that are taking place. This provides a warning to the people to take preventive and precautionary measures. The dataset of Karnataka region from 1951 to 2020 is used to study the regional climate change pattern. The main objective of the paper is to analyze the climate change and extending in the future. The results show that there is a gradual increase of average mean surface air temperature and gradual decrease of the precipitation over each decade between the years 1951 to 2020. The trend line extending to 2040 by analyzing the historical data gives insights about the climate change in the near future. Understanding the historical data and the future predictions are very important to the policy makers, people and researchers so that effective planning can be done for adapting and decreasing the climate change patterns.

articleTitle: Detection of Fusarium Wilt Disease in Pomegranate Plants using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: India is the world’s largest producer of pomegranates, but plant diseases significantly impact crop productivity, leading to major agricultural losses annually. Fusarium wilt, caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. ciceris (Foc), is one of the most common and severe diseases affecting pomegranate crops in India, reducing both the quantity and quality of production. Globally, Fusarium wilt poses a serious threat, with the potential to devastate entire fields under favorable conditions, causing up to ${1 0 0 \%}$ loss. Identifying this disease typically requires specialized knowledge or advanced systems. Deep learning (DL) is proposed as an effective method for disease recognition and classification due to its ability to extract features from images automatically. This study developed a deep learning model using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and a Softmax layer to classify pomegranate plant diseases. We collected 945 images directly from various farms in different cities, including Ballari, Bengaluru, and Bagalakote. Various image preprocessing techniques were applied, and data augmentation was used to prevent overfitting. The model was trained and evaluated on 3,000 images with data augmentation, with ${8 0 \%}$ of the images used for training and $20 \%$ for testing. The proposed integrated PomeNetV2 and ResNet50V2 CNN model demonstrated strong performance in identifying pomegranate plant diseases, achieving an accuracy of ${9 8 \%}$. The study concludes that the proposed CNN outperforms existing methods in disease detection and classification.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fault Detection in Industrial Process via a Hellinger Distance-Based Data-Driven Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Accurate fault detection in modern chemical processes ensures safety and efficiency. However, detecting faults in noisy environments remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces an effective fault detection (FD) strategy that combines a supervised learning approach using partial least squares (PLS) with fault detection charts based on Hellinger distance (HD) and exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA). The PLS-HD-EWMA strategy utilizes PLS to generate residuals, while HD is employed to compute the divergence between actual residuals and fault-free residuals. EWMA is then applied to evaluate the HD, providing sensitivity to small changes for effective fault detection. The proposed strategy’s efficacy is demonstrated through simulations on a benchmark continuous stirred tank reactor process, evaluating three common fault scenarios. The monitoring performance indicates that the PLS-HD-EWMA approach outperforms all the other conventional methods, offering superior fault detection capabilities.

articleTitle: Investigating Disruptions in Calcium Homeostasis in Neuron Cells Due to VOCC and NCX: Fuzzy Differential Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The concentration of calcium in the cytosol is influenced by many physiological processes, including calcium ion channel flow and buffering. Given the preceding, the main objective of this work is to create a model of the distribution of calcium in neural cells in the presence of an exchanger of sodium and calcium and a voltage-operated calcium channel. Reduced buffer levels and increased calcium activity in the voltage-operated calcium channel and exchanger of sodium and calcium are the root causes of neural diseases such as Alzheimer’s. Because of these changes, Alzheimer’s disease impacts and disrupts the calcium transport there. Furthermore, in situations where buffers are fully saturated or cannot bind calcium due to an anomaly or buffer damage, among other circumstances, the roles of voltage-operated calcium channels and exchanger of sodium and calcium in controlling the calcium concentration level become increasingly important. This study focuses on how calcium level changes in the presence of buffers, Endoplasmic Reticulum, voltage-operated calcium channels, and exchangers of sodium and calcium. Based on the physiological traits, appropriate boundary conditions have been developed in a fuzzy environment. The boundary conditions of this model are represented by triangular fuzzy functions, and it is addressed as a fuzzy boundary condition. Here, the approximated solution has been examined by using an undetermined fuzzy coefficient approach. An undetermined fuzzy coefficient approach is a technique for solving fuzzy differential equations that take uncertainty into account by predicting unknown coefficients as fuzzy numbers. To avoid cell loss in Alzheimer’s disease, the combined effect of all these parameters helps to maintain the calcium concentration.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Various Machine Learning Approaches to Predict Postoperative Mortality in Patients Undergoing Aortic Valve Replacement for Severe Aortic Stenosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Severe Aortic Stenosis (AS) is a life-threatening condition that progressively worsens with age and lifestyle factors, mainly affecting the elderly. In most cases, surgical intervention is required, followed by vigilant postoperative monitoring to ensure patient survival. This paper evaluates the predictive performance of eight machine learning algorithms in forecasting postoperative all-cause mortality in AS patients using two approaches: no resampling and resampling with the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) combined with Tomek Link removal. The predictive analysis incorporates two key cardiovascular biomarkers: hsTnT and NT-proBNP. Eight state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Classifier, k-nearest Neighbors, Decision Tree, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Random Forest, AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting, were evaluated for their predictive performance. Results show that AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting trained on resampled data outperformed others, achieving an accuracy of 0.78. The findings indicate the potential application of machine learning techniques in enhancing diagnostic and prognostic abilities for cardiovascular diseases as larger and more diverse datasets become available.

articleTitle: Short-term Wind Power Ramp Forecasting Using Sequential Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: As wind energy becomes a key player in the global transition to renewable energy, its variability presents significant challenges. Accurate wind ramp forecasting is crucial for managing such rapid fluctuations in wind power output, ensuring grid stability, and enhancing the reliability of renewable energy integration. This paper presents a short-term wind ramp forecasting model using a sequential approach: initially forecasting wind power through the integration of Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and the XGBoost algorithm, and subsequently detecting wind ramps using the Definition Based Sign Indicator (DSI) method. The historical wind speed and power data for Turkey was obtained from Kaggle. The dataset comprises readings from a wind turbine’s SCADA system in Turkey, with measurements recorded at 10minute intervals. Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) was applied to deconstruct and restore the historical wind power of the wind field, resulting in the formation of three training datasets. Wind power projections for the subsequent 8 hours, at 10 -minute intervals, are generated using historical wind power, wind speed, and wind direction as inputs. The DSI algorithm is employed to identify ramps. To assess the predictive capability of the proposed model, two algorithms, SVR and XGBoost, were employed for forecasting and the resulting error is minimal. The proposed model, VMD + XGBOOST is also compared without VMD to evaluate the performance. Taking mean square error (MSE), root mean square error (RMSE) mean absolute error (MAE), and symmetric mean absolute percentage error (sMAPE) as evaluation indicators, the results show that the forecasted accuracy of wind power is significantly improved after VMD processing. The performance of XGBOOST is better than SVR in the two evaluation indicators. Precision, Recall, and F1-score are calculated to evaluate the accuracy of the predicted wind ramps.

articleTitle: A Survey of 5G EMF, EMI Measurement, Health Impact and Shielding Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This study is a survey of 5G EMF and EMI measurement techniques, health impact, and novel shielding materials. Both computational and measured data are presented. Standards of safety and compliance discussed in prior works are included. Intra equipment shielding materials and human shielding fabrics are covered. Most international standards including ICNIRP have considered vulnerable population in establishing radiation limits. Though the immediate impact on human beings has not been established conclusively, the long term impact of radiation on the human body has not been studied thoroughly. Novel methods, processes shielding materials and fabrics are to be explored.

articleTitle: Exploring Transition Metal Doped Germanene for Enhanced Glucose Sensing: A DFT Study on Adsorption Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Diabetes, a chronic metabolic disorder, leads to high blood sugar levels and has been identified as one of the leading causes of mortality globally, emphasizing the need for improved glucose detection methods in medical diagnostics, food industry, and clinical settings. In this study, we explored the adsorption behavior of glucose on silver doped germanene and nickel doped germanene using Density Functional Theory. Metal doping significantly enhances germanene’s reactivity, increasing the strength of glucose adsorption. This is evident in the higher adsorption energies observed for metal-doped germanene, indicating stronger glucose interactions. The study involved analyzing key electronic properties, including charge transfer, band gap, Fermi energy, and work function. Metal doping in germanene induces substantial changes in the energygap upon glucose adsorption. High energygap variation in nickel doped germanene improves the electronic response, making it more sensitive to glucose molecules. Doping also modifies the work function of germanene, which plays a crucial role in work-function-based sensing mechanisms. Enhanced work function values in nickel doped germanene and silver doped germanene sheets enable better detection of glucose via work function shifts. Enhanced sensitivity and conductivity in nickel doped germanene sheets make them promising candidates for glucose sensing applications.

Author Keywords: Electronic properties and work function based sensor

articleTitle: Braille tactile representations in the brain: An EEG Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This study explores the neural correlates of braille tactile representations in individuals with visual impairments using electroencephalography. By examining both power spectral densities and event-related potentials, we aimed to understand how the brain processes braille tactile stimuli. The first study examined the effects of tactile processing on major frequency bands across different brain regions from either hand and individual braille letters. The results from the analysis identify that the left hemisphere is actively engaged in identifying, processing, and recognizing tactile stimuli. Increased alpha and theta band power suggest significant neuroplasticity changes in individuals with visual loss, indicating that the brain reallocates resources for efficient tactile information processing. Reduced beta and gamma power further support the brain’s optimized resource management during non-motor tactile activities. The second study involved event-related potentials analysis during the presentation of braille alphabets. The identification of $\mathrm{P} 1, \mathrm{P} 2$, and P300 patterns reveals that the brain is actively engaged in tactile processing and letter identification. The study demonstrates an underscoring potential for developing portable, wearable electronic Braille devices. Such advancements could facilitate simultaneous input of multiple characters, enhancing tactile processing speed and integrating visually impaired individuals into the broader communication landscape through Braille. Advancements in neural computing and brain computer interfaces should contribute to technology advancements in assistive tools like braille. Our results contribute to the understanding of sensory processing and cortical plasticity in the absence of vision, providing a foundation for future research and technology development aimed at improving Braille literacy and accessibility for the visually impaired.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach for State of Health Estimation in Lithium-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The lithium-ion battery (LIB) has become the most important energy storage solution due to the quick developments in Electric Vehicle (EV) technology. As a battery ages, its condition tends to steadily degrade and eventually loses its usability as a result of the unavoidable physiochemical reactions that occur inside it. The battery degradation can be estimated using State of Health (SOH). Accurate estimation of SOH of LIB application systems is a critical concern in the domain of EVs. To approximate the SOH of a battery, this study uses data-driven methodologies. An enormous amount of information, including temperature, current, and voltage, is obtained from the NASA Prognostics Centre of Excellence in order to evaluate health parameters. SOH estimation is carried out using four diverse ML techniques i.e. Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), and LSTM-GRU model. Though, the accuracy and performance of SOH prediction through these algorithms are extremely dependable on hyperparameter tuning. In this study, we compared the performance of LSTM, RNN, GRU, and a hybrid LSTM-GRU model in estimating SOH. The results indicate that the GRU model achieved the highest performance with an R2 score of 0.9577. Root Means Square Error (RMSE) values for LSTM, RNN, GRU, and hybrid LSTM-GRU models were $0.019,0.023,0.017$, and 0.019, respectively. These findings demonstrate the superior accuracy of the GRU model for SOH estimation of batteries.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Multi-Class Classification Models for Obesity Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Obesity is a global health issue associated with increased risks of various chronic diseases, such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and certain cancers. Accurate prediction of obesity risk can enable early interventions, improve patient outcomes, and alleviate healthcare burdens. This study performs a comparative analysis of several multiclass classification models to predict obesity risk levels based on demographic, lifestyle, and health-related features. we aimed to predict obesity risk in individuals using various machine learning algorithms, with a particular focus on the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM) classifier. Obesity is a growing global health issue linked to numerous serious diseases. We evaluated several algorithms, including LGBM, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Support Vector Classifier (SVC), Logistic Regression, and AdaBoost algorithms to determine their effectiveness in accurately classifying obesity risk. Our findings revealed that the LGBM classifier outperformed the others with an impressive accuracy of over $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$. Random Forest followed closely, while Decision Tree, SVC, Logistic Regression, and AdaBoost showed progressively lower accuracies. The LGBM algorithm’s superior performance highlights its potential as a valuable tool for early obesity risk detection and intervention, enabling healthcare providers to take proactive steps in managing and preventing obesity.

articleTitle: Emotion Privacy: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for Emotionally Enriched Video
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: As the use of video systems continues to expand across various domains, addressing privacy concerns while maintaining data integrity has become increasingly challenging. This paper introduces Emotion Privacy, a versatile framework that anonymizes faces in video feeds by replacing them with their own neutral faces. Unlike traditional anonymization techniques that primarily obscure identity but often fail to hide emotional data, our approach ensures compliance with privacy regulations by neutralizing emotional expressions. By applying neutral 3D face models in real time, we achieve complete emotional concealment, thus protecting emotional cues. Experimental validation reveals that Emotion Privacy achieves a great success in anonymization, ensuring that no emotional content can be inferred from the modified videos. This work presents a scalable, privacy-preserving solution that meets contemporary regulatory standards, offering broad applicability across diverse sectors where video content and privacy concerns intersect.

articleTitle: A Survey on Evolutionary Algorithms Based Machine Learning Approaches for Medical Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The use of extended time series to gather and store huge datasets has been made simpler by information science and data capture technologies. In many fields, such as astronomy, the environment, economics, business, medical, data analysis, and knowledge mining, these datasets are growing in popularity. Finding hidden patterns, connections, and anomalies in massive databases using statistical analysis and machine learning is known as data mining. You can use this information to help with comprehending complex phenomena, generating predictions, and making decision. The evolutionary computational techniques and machine learning techniques play a main role in the data mining process. This paper reviews various machine learning approaches that are based on different evolutionary algorithms such as genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization, and ant colony optimization for the classification of medical datasets. The comparison and discussion are made between different evolutionary algorithms-based techniques for the medical data classification process. The review of evolutionary algorithms-based classification approaches showed that the performance of evolutionary algorithms varied according to the medical datasets. The reviewed classification approaches also lead to the conclusion that evolutionary algorithms are essential for the data preprocessing and parameters tuning in machine learning based classifiers.

articleTitle: A Unified Framework for Dangerous Situation Detection by Integrating Weapon Detection and Distressed Face Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The escalating prevalence of violent threats necessitates proactive security measures to safeguard human life. Within the realm of artificial intelligence (AI), computer vision has emerged as a pivotal tool, leveraging sophisticated algorithms to substantially alleviate the burden on human resources. In this research work, we propose a novel approach for dangerous situation detection that combines object detection and facial emotion recognition. This work includes detecting guns, knives, blood, alcohol, insulting gestures, and cigarettes as these are considered as items that are commonly associated with potential threats or dangerous situations in various contexts, such as crime scenes, conflict zones, or public safety scenarios. To achieve this, the harmful object detection model employs YOLOv8, which has been successful based on the mAP metric. The proposed work also incorporates a CNN model that relies on facial emotions for indicators of distress, fear, or discomfort, enabling the system to identify potential threats even in scenarios devoid of harmful objects. The results obtained demonstrate YOLOv8’s superiority over a two-stage detector, and the Facial Expression Recognition (FER) CNN achieves $\mathbf{7 9 \%}$ test accuracy and $\mathbf{8 4 \%}$ validation accuracy. The unified framework enhances environmental threat detection, contributing to effective risk mitigation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Climate Change Understanding: A Novel Deep Learning Framework with the Climate Change Parameter Model(CCPM)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: One of the severe and pressing problems which humanity is facing in the 21st Century is climate change. It is adversely affecting the entire globe as is evident with the rising ocean levels, accelerated melting of glaciers, frequent storms, and many more. The need of the hour is to limit climate change by reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Machine learning algorithms have proven to be extremely effective in numerous scenarios and the experts are working to extend their uses to limit the effects of climate change. The domain is vast but in the current literature, the works in this domain are very limited. In this paper, we have tried to work in this particular direction by applying deep learning methodologies to analyze the effect of different climate factors on overall climate change. We proposed a novel climate change parameter model to predict the correlation between different climate parameters. We evaluated our scheme by validating the model on the data specific to the Jammu and Kashmir region and the model loss was found to be under $\mathbf{2 \%}$. In addition, based on our model we proposed some reactive strategies that can be implemented to keep the climate change effects under control.

articleTitle: Exploring Pupil Dilation as an Indicator of Performance in Gaze-Based Robot Navigation for Assistive Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Human-robot interaction (HRI) based assistive devices play a crucial role for individuals with severe disability, significantly impacting their quality of life. A pivotal step towards creating a more human-centric HRI involves gaining a thorough understanding of the user’s mental load such as cognitive load, stress, and fatigue, which can influence the performance of the system. Previous studies have found pupil dilation as a potential candidate for exploring mental workload. This paper explores the impact of pupil diameter variation on performance during an eye-tracking-based robot navigation task. Nineteen healthy individuals participated in the experiment where they used eye-gaze to activate different navigational buttons on a computer screen to control the movement of a mobile robot on a predefined trajectory for two rounds. The variation of pupil diameter is correlated to various performance parameters such as lap completion time and number of commands. Results show that the difference between the Gaussian means of the pupil diameter distribution during round1 and round2 is significantly correlated (rho $=0.5, p$-value $=0.03$) with the lap completion time while the correlation with the number of commands is also found to be strong ($\mathbf{r h o}=0.45$, $\mathbf{p}$-value $=0.05$). These quantifications of pupil diameter variations with performance measures have the potential to play a vital role in advancing the HRI systems as they can be used to predict the performance variation in real-time so that the HRI can be more responsive to the user’s changing mental states, a key requirement for the practical usability and acceptability of such systems as assistive technologies.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis of Low-Inertia Shipboard Electrical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Transient stability analysis (TSA) of synchronous generators (SGs) is essential for reliable operation of electrical systems. Conventionally, the equal area criterion (EAC) is used to assess the transient stability of SGs, assuming that they are connected to a bus with a fixed frequency. However, during disturbances in low-inertia systems, e.g., small microgrids and shipboard power systems, the frequency of the main ac bus may noticeably deviate. This paper proposes a new formulation within the EAC method for calculating the critical clearing time (CCT) of SGs in low-inertia electrical systems, considering the effect of variations in system frequency during TSA. To verify the effectiveness of the extended EAC, the CCTs of SGs in a multi-machine shipboard power system are obtained using the proposed formulation and compared with time-domain simulation results. The proposed EAC method estimates the CCTs more accurately when the main ac bus frequency varies following a disturbance.

articleTitle: Enhanced Medical Image Authentication and Precise Tamper Localization Using Discrete Cosine Stockwell Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Advancements in communication have boosted digital image sharing but also heightened security risks due to easy manipulation. Therefore, authentication techniques are crucial for securing medical images. This paper proposes a fully blind fragile watermarking model for color and grayscale medical image authentication and accurate tamper localization. The watermark is initially derived from the host image using the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and encrypted by a Logistic map-based technique to enhance the model’s security. The image is then divided into $4 \times 4$ blocks, and the Discrete Cosine Stockwell Transform (DCST) is performed on each block. Afterward, QR decomposition is performed on each frequency subband, and the watermark is inserted within the R matrices. Experimental results across various types of medical images indicate that the proposed technique provides high watermarked image quality with a Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR) exceeding 51dB while maintaining good embedding capacity and high sensitivity to attacks. Furthermore, the scheme achieves a highly accurate tamper localization, detecting tampering rates as low as $0.01 \%$ of the image size, which surpasses the accuracy achieved by other models in the literature.

articleTitle: A Disaster Prediction Ensemble Classifier Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Natural and man-made disasters may have severe impacts, but disaster prediction can help lessen such effects. The natural catastrophes that strike India on a regular basis cause immense devastation in terms of human lives and material possessions. Predicting the start and development of disasters in real-time is essential for reducing their effect. For more precise and trustworthy catastrophe predictions, this research presents an AI-powered catastrophe Ensemble B-Classifier network (DE BCN). The DPEC ensemble technique improves forecast accuracy over individual models by integrating various predictive outputs from numerous machine learning models that specialise in distinct kinds of disasters. This is where the data was originally pulled from Kaggle. To finish off the preprocessing, the norma clash filter was used. The next step is to use the optimisation method known as mustard twin swarm to extract characteristics that are connected to the tragedy. With any luck, the calamity Ensemble-B Classifier network will be able to forecast the calamity. Python and the Kaggle database were the environments used to carry out the investigation. According to the results of the simulations, the suggested approach is better than the current standard for predicting the catastrophic state.

articleTitle: Evaluating RF Data Transmission for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles for a Biomimicry Fish
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Underwater Wireless Communications (UWC) are extremely challenging. To understand and overcome this the paper examines the effectiveness of Radio Frequency (RF) data transmission for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs). A NodeMCU v3 ESP8266 board was used for this experiment to understand the bandwidth of 2.4 GHz RF communications in underwater environments. Key performance metrics like signal strength, latency, data loss, and speed were measured to understand the data transmissions. These findings highlight the challenges of RF signal underwater including attenuation and multipath effects. The results will help us understand the potential for real time sensor transmission that can be used in biomimicry of underwater robots. This will help us understand future advancements in RF, AUVs, and UWC technology.

articleTitle: LSTM and TCN based Hybrid Networks for Probabilistic Photovoltaic Power Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Rapid advancement in the photovoltaic industry, which provides sustainable energy resources for growing power demands worldwide, introduces unique grid integration and management challenges. With the stochastic nature of meteorological parameters, it is imperative to comprehend and analyze the characteristics of fluctuations thoroughly. Along with the massive technological evolution and significant potential of the PV sector, its dependability on intricate weather conditions can lead to substantial short-term variability in photovoltaic power, which significantly reduces the accuracy of deterministic prediction methods, causing an impact on the secure and stable operation of the power grid. This work proposes a short-term PV power prediction model based on feature extraction. The proposed model is built on efficient hybrid deep learning models: Temporal Convolution Network and Long-Short-Term Memory. Next, the prediction model is expanded to a probabilistic method by including Monte Carlo dropout and kernel density estimation to generate predictions of probability density. To evaluate the performance of the model, a dataset from the ‘Yulara Solar Project’ located in Australia is used, and a comparative and ablation study is conducted.

articleTitle: Enhancing seawater desalination plant Efficiency: Predicting treated water quality using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Reverse Osmosis is a widely adopted technology for seawater desalination, critical for addressing global water scarcity. As the demand for freshwater increases, the need for larger, more efficient desalination plants becomes imperative. Ensuring the quality of treated water that meets international human consumption standards requires precise knowledge of input parameters in the desalination process. This research investigates the application of deep learning techniques to predict the quality of treated water based on input parameters like the quality of input water, pressures of membranes, and ambient temperature. Utilizing data collected from 2022 to 2023, we evaluated various neural network architectures, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Residual Neural Networks (ResNet), and Visual Geometry Group networks (VGG). Our findings demonstrate that the Residual Neural Network architecture delivers the most accurate predictions. This approach facilitates real-time monitoring and adjustment of desalination parameters, thereby enhancing plant efficiency and potentially yielding significant improvements in performance and cost savings.

articleTitle: MetaIClone: A Robust Iris Clone Detection Mechanism for the Metaverse
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Recent advancements in artificial intelligence have paved the way for the metaverse to become an imminent reality. Within this virtual world, people can buy and sell virtual assets, meet up with friends, purchase goods, and attend event, all while using biometric traits for secure and seamless authentication. Iris recognition has become a highly prevalent method for human authentication due to its robustness and effectiveness. Despite its widespread use, these systems are vulnerable to various security threats, particularly when attackers use biometric replicas to impersonate legitimate users-commonly known as biometric cloning. To counteract such cloning attempts, an anti-cloning subsystem is incorporated with the sensor, enabling intelligent differentiation between genuine and clone iris traits. In this research, we present MetaIClone, a hybrid iris clone detection (ICD) system designed for secure identification within the metaverse. MetaIClone integrates the powerful features of two handcrafted feature extractors namely histogram of oriented gradient (HoG) and binary statistical image feature (BSIF), with the extracted feature vectors subsequently classified using two distinct support vector machines (SVMs). The final decision is achieved through score-level fusion with a fine-tuned MobileNet V2 model. We evaluated MetaIClone using benchmark datasets, including iris liveness detection Notre Dame 2017 (LivDet ND17) and Notre Dame cosmetic lenses dataset 2015 (NDCLD-15). Additionally, we introduced a digital clone generation technique using a generative adversarial network (GAN) model and tested the system on this novel dataset. MetaIClone excels in known attack scenarios, achieving an average classification error rate (ACER) of $\mathbf{0. 0 2 \%}$, and performs well in unseen attack scenarios with an ACER of $\mathbf{0. 0 5 \%}$, delivering competitive results in crossdatabase evaluations. Overall, MetaIClone outperforms other ICD models, offering superior accuracy with high computational efficiency.
